subject: English Grammar

entries.question_text: Choose the correct alternative to complete the sentence. ‘He —- to see us if he had been able to.’
entries.options_raw: ক) would come খ) may come গ) may have come ঘ) would have come
entries.explanation: এটি একটি Third Conditional Sentence। এর গঠন হলো: If + Past Perfect, would have + past participle (V3)। যেহেতু if-clause টি 'had been' (Past Perfect) এ আছে, তাই main clause টি 'would have come' হবে।

entries.question_text: Choose the appropriate alternative to complete the sentence. ‘He had a—of fever.’
entries.options_raw: ক) strong attack খ) severe attack গ) serious kind ঘ) bad attack
entries.explanation: রোগের তীব্রতা বা ভয়াবহতা বোঝাতে 'severe attack' একটি উপযুক্ত collocation (শব্দগুচ্ছ)। 'Severe' অর্থ তীব্র বা মারাত্মক। তাই 'He had a severe attack of fever' অর্থ তিনি প্রচণ্ড জ্বরে আক্রান্ত হয়েছিলেন।

entries.question_text: Choose the correct sentence.

options.label: ক
options.text: I asked Javed had he passed

options.label: খ
options.text: I asked Javed if he had passed

options.label: গ
options.text: I asked Javed if you had passed

options.label: ঘ
options.text: I asked Javed that had he passed

entries.options_raw: ক) I asked Javed had he passed খ) I asked Javed if he had passed গ) I asked Javed if you had passed ঘ) I asked Javed that had he passed
entries.correct_answer: খ) I asked Javed if he had passed
entries.explanation: এটি একটি Indirect Speech। Interrogative sentence-কে indirect করার সময় reporting verb 'asked' এর পর 'if' বা 'whether' বসে এবং subsequent clause-টি assertive form-এ (Subject + Verb) হয়। তাই সঠিক বাক্যটি হলো 'I asked Javed if he had passed'।

entries.question_text: Choose the correct answer. How long did you wait?
entries.options_raw: ক) Till lunch time. খ) Till he came. গ) Until six o’clock. ঘ) Since this morning.
entries.explanation: প্রশ্নটি 'How long' (কতক্ষণ) দিয়ে করা হয়েছে, যা একটি সময়কাল জানতে চায়। 'Till' বা 'Until' দিয়ে কোনো কাজের শেষ সময় নির্দেশ করা হয়। এখানে 'Till he came' (যতক্ষণ না সে আসল) একটি পূর্ণাঙ্গ adverbial clause of time যা প্রশ্নের সঠিক ও সম্পূর্ণ উত্তর প্রদান করে। অন্য অপশনগুলোও সময় নির্দেশক, কিন্তু এটি ব্যাকরণগতভাবে সবচেয়ে সুগঠিত উত্তর।

entries.question_text: What will be the correct preposition to complete the sentence? ‘I am not bad-tennis’.
entries.options_raw: ক) in খ) at গ) about ঘ) with
entries.explanation: কোনো বিষয়ে দক্ষ বা অদক্ষ বোঝাতে good/bad এর পর 'at' preposition টি ব্যবহৃত হয়। যেমন: good at English, bad at mathematics। সুতরাং সঠিক বাক্যটি হলো 'I am not bad at tennis'।

entries.question_text: What is the antonym of ‘Gentle’?
entries.options_raw: ক) Harsh খ) Modest গ) Clever ঘ) Rude
entries.explanation: 'Gentle' অর্থ নম্র, ভদ্র বা শান্ত। এর বিপরীত শব্দ হলো 'Rude' যার অর্থ অভদ্র, রূঢ়। 'Harsh' (কর্কশ) কাছাকাছি হলেও, আচরণগত বৈপরীত্য বোঝাতে 'Rude' সবচেয়ে উপযুক্ত।

entries.question_text: What is the synonym of ‘Jovial’?
entries.options_raw: ক) Jolly খ) Gay গ) Jealous ঘ) Happy
entries.explanation: 'Jovial' অর্থ হাসিখুশি, আমুদে। 'Jolly', 'Gay' (এখানে পুরনো অর্থে 'আমুদে'), এবং 'Happy' তিনটি শব্দই 'Jovial' এর সমার্থক। একাধিক সঠিক উত্তর থাকায় প্রশ্নটি বাতিল করা হয়।

entries.question_text: What is the synonym of ‘Competent’?
entries.options_raw: ক) Circumspect খ) Discrete গ) Capable ঘ) Prudent
entries.explanation: 'Competent' অর্থ সক্ষম, যোগ্য বা উপযুক্ত। এর সরাসরি সমার্থক শব্দ হলো 'Capable', যার অর্থও সক্ষম বা সমর্থ।

entries.question_text: Who is the author of ‘A Farewell to Arms’?
entries.options_raw: ক) H. G. Wells খ) George Orwel গ) Thomas Hardy ঘ) Ernest Hemingway
entries.explanation: 'A Farewell to Arms' (1929) হলো আমেরিকান লেখক আর্নেস্ট হেমিংওয়ের লেখা একটি বিখ্যাত উপন্যাস, যা প্রথম বিশ্বযুদ্ধের প্রেক্ষাপটে রচিত।

entries.question_text: Who is the author of ‘Animal Farm’?
entries.options_raw: ক) Thomas More খ) George Orwel গ) Boris Pasternak ঘ) Charles Dickens
entries.explanation: 'Animal Farm' (1945) ব্রিটিশ লেখক জর্জ অরওয়েলের একটি বিখ্যাত রূপকধর্মী উপন্যাস, যা রাশিয়ার স্তালিনবাদী শাসনের বিরুদ্ধে একটি স্যাটায়ার।

entries.question_text: Who is the author of ‘India Wins Freedom’?
entries.options_raw: ক) Mahatma Gandhi খ) J. L. Nehru গ) Abul Kalam Azad ঘ) Moulana Akram Khan
entries.explanation: 'India Wins Freedom' হলো ভারতের স্বাধীনতা সংগ্রামী ও প্রথম শিক্ষামন্ত্রী আবুল কালাম আজাদের লেখা একটি আত্মজীবনীমূলক গ্রন্থ।

entries.question_text: What kind of noun is ‘Cattle’?
entries.options_raw: ক) Proper খ) Common গ) Collective ঘ) Material
entries.explanation: Collective Noun হলো সেই noun যা একজাতীয় কতগুলো ব্যক্তি বা বস্তুকে পৃথকভাবে না বুঝিয়ে তাদের সমষ্টিকে বোঝায়। 'Cattle' (গবাদি পশু) শব্দটি দ্বারা অনেকগুলো গরুর সমষ্টিকে বোঝানো হয়, তাই এটি একটি Collective Noun।

entries.question_text: What kind of noun is ‘Girl’?
entries.options_raw: ক) Proper খ) Common গ) Collective ঘ) Material
entries.explanation: Common Noun এক জাতীয় ব্যক্তি বা বস্তুর সাধারণ নামকে বোঝায়। 'Girl' (বালিকা) শব্দটি দ্বারা কোনো নির্দিষ্ট বালিকাকে না বুঝিয়ে যেকোনো বালিকাকে বোঝায়, তাই এটি একটি Common Noun।

entries.question_text: What is the meaning of ‘White Elephant’?

options.label: খ
options.text: A very coslty or troublesome possession

entries.options_raw: ক) An elephant of white colour খ) A very coslty or troublesome possession গ) A black marketer ঘ) A hoarder
entries.correct_answer: খ) A very coslty or troublesome possession
entries.explanation: 'A white elephant' একটি idiom, যার অর্থ এমন কোনো বস্তু যা অত্যন্ত মূল্যবান বা ব্যয়বহুল কিন্তু মালিকের জন্য বোঝা বা ঝামেলাস্বরূপ এবং কোনো কাজে আসে না।

entries.question_text: What is the synonym of ‘Incite’?
entries.options_raw: (ক) Instigate (খ) Permit (গ) Urge (ঘ) Deceive
entries.explanation: Incite অর্থ উস্কানি দেওয়া বা প্ররোচিত করা। Instigate অর্থও প্ররোচিত করা বা উত্তেজিত করা। তাই এরা সমার্থক। Permit - অনুমতি দেওয়া, Urge - অনুরোধ করা, Deceive - প্রতারণা করা।

entries.question_text: What is the antonym of ‘Honorary’?
entries.options_raw: (ক) Official (খ) Honorable (গ) Salaried (ঘ) Literary
entries.explanation: Honorary অর্থ অবৈতনিক বা সম্মানসূচক (যে পদের জন্য কোনো বেতন দেওয়া হয় না)। এর বিপরীত শব্দ হলো Salaried, যার অর্থ বেতনভুক্ত।

entries.question_text: What is the verb of the word ‘Ability’?
entries.options_raw: (ক) Ableness (খ) Able (গ) Ably (ঘ) Enable
entries.explanation: Ability (noun) অর্থ সামর্থ্য। এর verb form হলো Enable, যার অর্থ সক্ষম করা। Able একটি adjective (সক্ষম) এবং Ably একটি adverb (সক্ষমতার সাথে)।

entries.question_text: Who is the poet of the ‘Victorian Age’?
entries.options_raw: (ক) Helen Keller (খ) Mathew Arnold (গ) Shakespeare (ঘ) Robert Browning
entries.explanation: ভিক্টোরিয়ান যুগের (১৮৩৭-১৯০১) কবিদের মধ্যে Mathew Arnold এবং Robert Browning উভয়ই অন্তর্ভুক্ত। প্রশ্নে দুটি সঠিক উত্তর থাকায় এটি বাতিল করা হয়েছে। শেক্সপিয়র ছিলেন Elizabethan যুগের কবি।

entries.question_text: Who is the author of ‘For Whom the Bell Tolls’?
entries.options_raw: (ক) Charles Dickens (খ) Homer (গ) Lord Tennyson (ঘ) Ernest Hemingway
entries.explanation: 'For Whom the Bell Tolls' মার্কিন সাহিত্যিক আর্নেস্ট হেমিংওয়ের লেখা একটি বিখ্যাত উপন্যাস। এটি اسپেনের গৃহযুদ্ধের প্রেক্ষাপটে রচিত।

entries.question_text: Fill in the blank ‘He has assured me _____ safety.’
entries.options_raw: (ক) with (খ) at (গ) for (ঘ) of
entries.explanation: Assure somebody of something একটি উপযুক্ত Prepositional Phrase, যার অর্থ কোনো বিষয়ে কাউকে আশ্বস্ত করা। এখানে নিরাপত্তার বিষয়ে আশ্বস্ত করার জন্য 'of' ব্যবহৃত হবে।

entries.question_text: ‘May Allah help you’ What kind of sentence is this?
entries.options_raw: (ক) Optative (খ) Imperative (গ) Assertive (ঘ) Exclamatory
entries.explanation: যে বাক্য দ্বারা কোনো ইচ্ছা, প্রার্থনা বা আকাঙ্ক্ষা প্রকাশ পায়, তাকে Optative Sentence বলে। 'May Allah help you' একটি প্রার্থনা, তাই এটি Optative Sentence।

entries.question_text: A rolling stone gathers no moss. What ‘rolling’ is?
entries.options_raw: (ক) Gerund (খ) Verbal noun (গ) Participle (ঘ) Adjective
entries.explanation: এখানে 'rolling' শব্দটি 'stone' (noun) কে വിശേഷিত করছে (কেমন পাথর? - ঘূর্ণায়মান পাথর)। Verb-এর ing-যুক্ত রূপ যখন Adjective-এর মতো কাজ করে, তখন তাকে Participle বলে।

entries.question_text: ‘He has been ill _____ Friday last’ fill in the blank.
entries.options_raw: (ক) Since (খ) In (গ) From (ঘ) On
entries.explanation: Present Perfect Continuous Tense-এর ক্ষেত্রে কোনো নির্দিষ্ট সময় (point of time) থেকে কাজ চলছে বোঝালে 'since' ব্যবহৃত হয়। 'Friday last' একটি নির্দিষ্ট সময়।

entries.question_text: Which is the noun form of the word ‘beautiful’?
entries.options_raw: (ক) Beauteous (খ) Beauty (গ) Beautifully (ঘ) Beautify
entries.explanation: Beautiful (Adjective) অর্থ সুন্দর। এর Noun form হলো Beauty (সৌন্দর্য)। Beautify হলো Verb (সুন্দর করা) এবং Beautifully হলো Adverb (সুন্দরভাবে)।

entries.question_text: ‘Hold water’ means-
entries.options_raw: (ক) Keep water (খ) Drink water (গ) Bear examination (ঘ) Store water
entries.explanation: 'Hold water' একটি idiom, যার অর্থ যুক্তিসঙ্গত বা টেকসই হওয়া, পরীক্ষায় টিকে থাকা। 'Bear examination' অর্থ যাচাই বা পরীক্ষায় টিকে থাকা, যা এই idiom-টির অর্থের কাছাকাছি।

entries.question_text: ‘Out and Out’ means-
entries.options_raw: (ক) Not at all (খ) Thoroughly (গ) To be last (ঘ) Man of outside
entries.explanation: 'Out and out' একটি idiom, যার অর্থ সম্পূর্ণরূপে বা আগাগোড়া। Thoroughly শব্দের অর্থও সম্পূর্ণরূপে।

entries.question_text: Choose the correct sentence-

options.label: খ
options.text: The rich is not always happy

options.label: গ
options.text: The rich is not happy always

options.label: ঘ
options.text: The rich are not always happy

entries.options_raw: (ক) Rich is not always happy (খ) The rich is not always happy (গ) The rich is not happy always (ঘ) The rich are not always happy
entries.correct_answer: (ঘ) The rich are not always happy
entries.explanation: Adjective-এর পূর্বে 'The' বসলে তা Plural Common Noun-এ পরিণত হয় এবং Plural verb গ্রহণ করে। 'The rich' অর্থ ধনীরা, তাই এরপর 'are' বসবে।

entries.question_text: Choose the correct sentence –

options.label: ক
options.text: He had been hunged for murder

options.label: খ
options.text: He has been hunged for murder

entries.options_raw: (ক) He had been hunged for murder (খ) He has been hunged for murder (গ) He was hanged for murder (ঘ) He was hunged of murder
entries.explanation: 'Hang' verb-টির দুটি রূপ আছে। ফাঁসিতে ঝোলানো অর্থে এর past form হলো 'hanged'। কোনো বস্তু ঝোলানো অর্থে past form হলো 'hung'। যেহেতু এখানে খুনের জন্য ফাঁসির কথা বলা হচ্ছে, 'hanged' সঠিক।

entries.question_text: ‘Syntax’ means –
entries.options_raw: (ক) Manner of speech (খ) Sentence building (গ) Supplementary tax (ঘ) Synchronizing act
entries.explanation: Syntax বা বাক্যতত্ত্ব হলো ব্যাকরণের সেই অংশ যেখানে বাক্য গঠনের নিয়মাবলী (rules of sentence building) আলোচনা করা হয়।

entries.question_text: ‘Justice delayed is justice denied’ was stated by –
entries.options_raw: (ক) Disraeli (খ) Emerson (গ) Gladstone (ঘ) Shakespeare
entries.explanation: 'বিচারের বিলম্ব মানে বিচার অস্বীকার করা'— এই বিখ্যাত উক্তিটি ব্রিটিশ প্রধানমন্ত্রী উইলিয়াম ইওয়ার্ট গ্ল্যাডস্টোনের (William Ewart Gladstone)।

entries.question_text: What is the verb form of the word ‘Shortly’?
entries.options_raw: (a) Short (b) Shorter (c) Shorten (d) Shortness
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Shortly' is an adverb. 'Short' is an adjective. 'Shorter' is the comparative form of the adjective. 'Shortness' is a noun. 'Shorten' is the verb, which means to make something shorter.

entries.question_text: Choose the correct sentence-

options.label: a
options.text: Let he and you be witnesses

options.label: b
options.text: Let you and him be witnesses

options.label: c
options.text: Let you and he be witnesses

options.label: d
options.text: Let you and he be witnesses

entries.options_raw: (a) Let he and you be witnesses (b) Let you and him be witnesses (c) Let you and he be witnesses (d) Let you and he be witnesses
entries.correct_answer: (b) Let you and him be witnesses
entries.explanation: Explanation: The verb 'Let' is always followed by a pronoun in the objective case (e.g., me, us, you, him, her, it, them). The objective form of 'he' is 'him'. Therefore, 'you and him' is the correct form.

entries.question_text: Who, Which, What are-
entries.options_raw: (a) Demonstrative pronoun (b) Relative pronoun (c) Reflexive pronoun (d) Indefinite pronoun
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Who', 'which', and 'what' can be used to introduce a relative clause, connecting it to the main clause. In this function, they are known as relative pronouns. They can also be interrogative pronouns when used to ask questions.

entries.question_text: Choose the correct one-
entries.options_raw: (a) Mispel (b) Misspell (c) Mispell (d) Misspel
entries.explanation: Explanation: The correct spelling is 'misspell', which means to spell a word incorrectly. It is formed by adding the prefix 'mis-' to the word 'spell'.

entries.question_text: Fill in the blank: ‘What is the time ___ your watch?’
entries.options_raw: (a) by (b) in (c) at (d) With
entries.explanation: Explanation: The standard preposition to use when asking for the time as shown on a watch or clock is 'by'. "What is the time by your watch?" is the correct idiomatic expression.

entries.question_text: Fill in the blank: ‘Give my _____ to him.’
entries.options_raw: (a) Warm compliment (b) Compliments (c) Best compliment (d) Heartiest compliment
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Compliments' (in the plural form) is an expression of praise, admiration, or respect. The phrase "Give my compliments to him" is a standard way of sending greetings or regards to someone.

entries.question_text: ‘Caesar and Cleopatra’ is-

options.label: b
options.text: a play by G. B. Shaw

options.label: d
options.text: a novel by S. T. Coleridge

entries.options_raw: (a) a tragedy by Shakespeare (b) a play by G. B. Shaw (c) a poem by Lord Byron (d) a novel by S. T. Coleridge
entries.correct_answer: (b) a play by G. B. Shaw
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Caesar and Cleopatra' is a historical play written in 1898 by the Irish playwright George Bernard Shaw. It depicts the relationship between Julius Caesar and Cleopatra, Queen of Egypt.

entries.question_text: Who is the greatest modern English dramatist?
entries.options_raw: (a) Verginia Woolf (b) George Bernard Shaw (c) P. B. Shelley (d) S. T. Coleridge
entries.explanation: Explanation: George Bernard Shaw is widely regarded as one of the most significant and influential English-language dramatists of the modern era, second only to Shakespeare. He was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1925.

entries.question_text: Who is the modern philosopher who was awarded the Nobel Prize for literature?
entries.options_raw: (a) James Baker (b) Dr. Kissinger (c) Bertrand Russel (d) Lenin
entries.explanation: Explanation: Bertrand Russell, a British philosopher, logician, mathematician, and social critic, was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1950 "in recognition of his varied and significant writings in which he champions humanitarian ideals and freedom of thought."

entries.question_text: Who is the author of ‘A Farewell to Arms’?
entries.options_raw: (a) T. S. Eliot (b) John Milton (c) Plato (d) Ernest Hemingway
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'A Farewell to Arms' is a novel by American writer Ernest Hemingway, published in 1929. It is set during the Italian campaign of World War I.

entries.question_text: Who is the most famous satirist in English literature?
entries.options_raw: (a) Alexander Pope (b) Jonathan Swift (c) William Wordsworth (d) Bulter
entries.explanation: Explanation: Jonathan Swift, the author of 'Gulliver's Travels' and 'A Modest Proposal', is considered the foremost satirist in the English language. His works masterfully use irony, wit, and sarcasm to critique politics, religion, and human nature.

entries.question_text: What is the synonym of ‘Delude’?
entries.options_raw: (a) Demand (b) Permit (c) Aggravate (d) Deceive
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'To delude' means to mislead the mind or judgment of someone, to make them believe something that is not true. 'Deceive' has a very similar meaning, which is to cause someone to believe something that is not true, typically in order to gain some personal advantage.

entries.question_text: What is the noun form of the word ‘Waste’?
entries.options_raw: (a) Waste (b) Wasting (c) Wastage (d) Wasteful
entries.explanation: Explanation: Both 'waste' and 'wastage' can be nouns. However, 'waste' refers to the unwanted material itself, while 'wastage' refers to the action or process of wasting something or the amount wasted. In this context, 'wastage' is the more appropriate abstract noun form derived from the verb 'to waste'.

entries.question_text: What is the antonym of ‘Queer’?
entries.options_raw: (a) Integrated (b) Orderly (c) Abnormal (d) Odd
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Queer' means strange, odd, or unusual. Its antonym would be something normal, regular, or systematic. Among the given options, 'Orderly' (meaning neat, systematic, or well-behaved) is the best antonym. 'Abnormal' and 'Odd' are synonyms.

entries.question_text: What is the adjective of the word ‘Heart’?
entries.options_raw: (a) Heart (b) Hearten (c) Heartening (d) Heartful
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Heart' is a noun. 'To hearten' is a verb meaning to make more cheerful or confident. 'Heartening' is the present participle of the verb, which is used as an adjective meaning something that is encouraging or makes one feel cheerful (e.g., 'heartening news').

entries.question_text: Select the answer of the word ‘stagflation’.
entries.options_raw: (a) controlled prices (b) economic slow down (c) a disintegrating government (d) Cultural dullness
entries.explanation: Explanation: Stagflation is a term in economics used to describe a situation where the inflation rate is high, the economic growth rate slows down (stagnation), and unemployment remains steadily high. 'Economic slow down' is a key component of this phenomenon.

entries.question_text: What is the meaning of the word ‘scuttle’?
entries.options_raw: (a) to tease (b) abandon (c) pile up (d) gossip
entries.explanation: Explanation: The word 'scuttle' has two main meanings. One is to run with short, quick steps. The other, more figurative meaning, is to deliberately cause a plan, scheme, or proposal to fail or be abandoned. In this context, 'abandon' is the closest synonym.

entries.question_text: What is the meaning of the word ‘stanch’?
entries.options_raw: (a) to reinforce (b) be weak (c) smooth out (d) put an end to
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Stanch' (also spelled 'staunch') means to stop or restrict the flow of something, typically blood from a wound. By extension, it means to stop something from continuing, i.e., to put an end to it.

entries.question_text: What is the meaning of the word ‘belated’?
entries.options_raw: (a) complaining (b) off hand (c) weak (d) tardy
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Belated' means coming or happening later than should have been the case. 'Tardy' also means delaying or delayed beyond the right or expected time. They are synonyms.

entries.question_text: What is the meaning of the word ‘sequences’?
entries.options_raw: (a) to follow (b) round up (c) withdraw (d) question closely
entries.explanation: Explanation: A 'sequence' is a particular order in which related events, movements, or things follow each other. The verb form implies things that follow in a series. Therefore, 'to follow' captures the essence of the word.

entries.question_text: What is the meaning of the word ‘euphemism’?
entries.options_raw: (a) vague idea (b) in offensive expression (c) verbal play (d) wise saying
entries.explanation: Explanation: A euphemism is a mild or indirect word or expression substituted for one considered to be too harsh, blunt, or embarrassing. It is an inoffensive way of saying something unpleasant.

entries.question_text: ‘The rainbow’ is-

options.label: b
options.text: a short story by Somerset Maugham

options.label: c
options.text: a novel by D. H. Lawrence

entries.options_raw: (a) a poem by Wordsworth (b) a short story by Somerset Maugham (c) a novel by D. H. Lawrence (d) a verse by Coleridge
entries.correct_answer: (c) a novel by D. H. Lawrence
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'The Rainbow' (1915) is a famous and controversial novel by the English author D. H. Lawrence. Wordsworth wrote a poem titled "My Heart Leaps Up," which is often referred to by its first line, "My heart leaps up when I behold a rainbow in the sky," but 'The Rainbow' itself is Lawrence's novel.

entries.question_text: ‘Tom Jones’ by Henry Fielding was first published in-
entries.options_raw: (a) the 1st half of 19th century (b) the 2nd half of 18th century (c) the 1st half of 18th century (d) the 2nd half of 19th century
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'The History of Tom Jones, a Foundling', commonly known as 'Tom Jones', is a comic novel by Henry Fielding. It was first published in 1749, which falls in the first half of the 18th century.

entries.question_text: The literary work ‘Kubla Khan’ is-

options.label: d
options.text: a short story by Somerset Maugham

entries.options_raw: (a) a history by Vincent Smith (b) a verse by Coleridge (c) a drama by Oscar Wilde (d) a short story by Somerset Maugham
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Kubla Khan; or, A Vision in a Dream: A Fragment' is a famous poem (verse) by the English Romantic poet Samuel Taylor Coleridge, composed in 1797.

entries.question_text: T. S Eliot was born in-
entries.options_raw: (a) Ireland (b) England (c) Wales (d) USA
entries.explanation: Explanation: Thomas Stearns (T. S.) Eliot was born in St. Louis, Missouri, USA, in 1888. Although he moved to England in 1914 and became a British subject in 1927, he was American by birth.

entries.question_text: What was the real name of the great American short writer, ‘O Henry’?
entries.options_raw: (a) Samuel L. Clemen (b) William Sydney Porter (c) Fitz-James O’Brien (d) William Huntington Wright
entries.explanation: Explanation: O. Henry was the pen name of the American short-story writer William Sydney Porter. Samuel L. Clemens was the real name of Mark Twain.

entries.question_text: Anything ‘Pernicious’ tends to injure or destroy. Something which has no such harmful effect is-
entries.options_raw: (a) innocuous (b) innocent (c) immaculate (d) salutary
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Pernicious' means having a harmful effect, especially in a gradual or subtle way. The opposite would be something harmless. 'Innocuous' means not harmful or offensive. 'Salutary' means beneficial, which is also an antonym but 'innocuous' is a more direct opposite to 'harmful'.

entries.question_text: Do not worry, English grammar is not ____ to understand. Which of the following best fits in the blank space.
entries.options_raw: (a) so difficult (b) very difficult (c) too difficult (d) difficult enough
entries.explanation: Explanation: The structure 'too + adjective + to + verb' is used to mean that something is excessively difficult, preventing a certain action. The sentence implies that it's not so difficult that it can't be understood. Thus, "not too difficult to understand" is the correct and idiomatic construction.

entries.question_text: We (not have) a holiday since the beginning of the year.- Which of the following verb forms best completes the above sentence?
entries.options_raw: (a) did not have (b) have not had (c) are not having (d) had not had
entries.explanation: Explanation: The use of 'since' indicates a period of time from a point in the past until the present. This requires the use of the Present Perfect tense. The present perfect form of '(not have)' is 'have not had'.

entries.question_text: If I were you, I (handle) the situation more carefully. -Which of the following verb forms best completes the above sentence?
entries.options_raw: (a) would handle (b) will handle (c) handle (d) would have handled
entries.explanation: Explanation: This is a second conditional sentence, which describes an unreal or hypothetical situation in the present or future. The structure is 'If + simple past, ... would + base verb'. Therefore, 'If I were you, I would handle...' is the correct form.

entries.question_text: It’s time (you realize) your mistakes. Which of the following clause best fits in the above sentence?
entries.options_raw: (a) you realized (b) that you realize (c) you would realize (d) you have realized
entries.explanation: Explanation: The expression 'It's time' or 'It's high time' is followed by a subject and a verb in the simple past tense to indicate that something should be done now or should have been done already. So, 'It's time you realized...' is correct.

entries.question_text: We have recently entered _____ an agreement with the Island co-operative society.
entries.options_raw: (a) no preposition (b) upon (c) in (d) into
entries.explanation: Explanation: The phrasal verb 'enter into' means to start to become involved in a formal arrangement, agreement, or discussion. When 'enter' means physical entry (e.g., enter a room), it doesn't take a preposition. For agreements, 'into' is the correct preposition.

entries.question_text: The boy from the village said, ”I ___ starve than beg.”- Which of the following best completes the above sentence?
entries.options_raw: (a) better (b) rather (c) would rather (d) would better
entries.explanation: Explanation: The structure 'would rather + verb (base form) + than + verb (base form)' is used to express a preference. The boy is stating his preference to starve over begging. 'Had better' is used for advice, not preference.

entries.question_text: It is too difficult to ‘tolerate’ bad temper for long.- Which of the following phrases best replaces ‘tolerate’ in the above sentence?
entries.options_raw: (a) cope up with (b) put up with (c) stand up for (d) pull on with
entries.explanation: Explanation: The phrasal verb 'put up with' means to tolerate or endure something or someone patiently. It is a direct synonym for 'tolerate'. 'Cope up with' is an incorrect phrase; the correct one is 'cope with'.

entries.question_text: I have never seen such a slow coach like you, this small work has taken you three full months.-What does the idiom ‘a slow coach’ mean?
entries.options_raw: (a) an irresponsible person (b) a careless person (c) an unthoughtful person (d) a very lazy person
entries.explanation: Explanation: The idiom 'a slowcoach' (usually one word) refers to a person who acts or moves slowly, or is lazy and falls behind in their work or tasks.

entries.question_text: You should show good manners in the company of young ladies. -Which is the appropriate phrase for the underlined expression above?
entries.options_raw: (a) behave gently (b) practise manners (c) behave yourself (d) do not talk rudely
entries.explanation: Explanation: To "show good manners" means to act politely and respectfully. "Behave gently" is the closest synonym among the choices, conveying the sense of politeness and consideration.

entries.question_text: The invention of computer has turned over a new leaf in the history of modern technology. -Which of the following is nearest in meaning of the italicized idiom above?
entries.options_raw: (a) Created a new history (b) began a new civiliztion (c) opened a new chapter (d) created a sensation
entries.explanation: Explanation: The idiom "to turn over a new leaf" means to start behaving in a better way or to begin something new and different. In this context, it signifies starting a new phase or chapter in the history of technology.

entries.question_text: Trying unitedly we were able to have our project approved against strong oppositions. -Which of the following says nearly the same as ‘against’ above?
entries.options_raw: (a) in the wake of (b) in the guise of (c) in the plea of (d) in the teeth of
entries.explanation: Explanation: The phrase "in the teeth of" means in direct opposition to or despite. It perfectly replaces "against" in the context of overcoming strong opposition.

entries.question_text: Not many people can commit such a heinous crime in cold blood. -What does the italicized idiom above mean?

options.label: a
options.text: in cool brain and calculated thought

entries.options_raw: (a) in cool brain and calculated thought (b) so patiently and thoughtfully (c) so impatiently and thoughtlessly (d) stirred by sudden emotion
entries.correct_answer: (a) in cool brain and calculated thought
entries.explanation: Explanation: The idiom "in cold blood" means to do something cruelly, deliberately, and without emotion. "In cool brain and calculated thought" accurately describes this state of mind.

entries.question_text: The condition of most slum dwellers is so miserable that it cannot be described in words.- Which is the best phrase for the underlined expression above?
entries.options_raw: (a) beggars description (b) cuts to the quick (c) boils down to this (d) keeps open house
entries.explanation: Explanation: The idiom "beggars description" means to be too extreme, shocking, or beautiful to be described in words. It perfectly fits the context of the slum dwellers' miserable condition.

entries.question_text: A speech full of too many word is-
entries.options_raw: (a) A big speech (b) Maiden speech (c) An unimportant speech (d) A verbose speech
entries.explanation: Explanation: The word 'verbose' means using or expressed in more words than are needed. Therefore, a speech with too many words is a verbose speech.

entries.question_text: To meet trouble half-way means-
entries.options_raw: (a) To be puzzled (b) To get nervous (c) To be disappointed (d) To bear up
entries.explanation: Explanation: The idiom "to meet trouble halfway" means to worry about problems before they actually happen, or to take unnecessary steps to avoid them, often leading to anxiety and confusion. 'To be puzzled' or 'to get nervous' are close in meaning, but 'to be puzzled' captures the sense of being confused by worrying in advance.

entries.question_text: ‘Paradise Lost’ attempted to-

options.label: a
options.text: Justify the ways of man to God

options.label: b
options.text: Justify the ways of God to man

options.label: c
options.text: Show that the Satan and God have equal power

options.label: d
options.text: Explain why good and evil are necessary

entries.options_raw: (a) Justify the ways of man to God (b) Justify the ways of God to man (c) Show that the Satan and God have equal power (d) Explain why good and evil are necessary
entries.correct_answer: (b) Justify the ways of God to man
entries.explanation: Explanation: In the opening lines of his epic poem 'Paradise Lost', John Milton explicitly states his purpose is to "assert Eternal Providence, / And justify the ways of God to men."

entries.question_text: What is the meaning of the idiom ‘a round dozen’?

options.label: a
options.text: a little less than a dozen

options.label: b
options.text: a little more than a dozen

entries.options_raw: (a) a little less than a dozen (b) a little more than a dozen (c) a full dozen (d) round about a dozen
entries.explanation: Explanation: The idiom 'a round dozen' means exactly twelve, a complete or full dozen.

entries.question_text: What is the meaning of ‘Soft Soap’?
entries.options_raw: (a) Flatter for self motives (b) To speak ill of others (c) To speak high of others (d) To recognise about a dozen
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Soft soap' is an idiom that means to use flattery or persuasive talk to get what you want from someone.

entries.question_text: People who assume that no evil can befall them are foolishly-
entries.options_raw: (a) ardent (b) complacent (c) confident (d) apprehensive
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Complacent' describes someone who feels smug and uncritical satisfaction with themselves or their situation, often unaware of potential dangers. This word perfectly fits the description of being foolishly overconfident.

entries.question_text: One who unduly forwards in rendering serving for others is not generally liked in society.- Which of the following words represents truely the character of the person mentioned above?
entries.options_raw: (a) benevolent (b) official (c) officious (d) burreaucratic
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Officious' means annoyingly eager to help or advise; meddlesome. It accurately describes someone who is overly forward in offering unwanted services.

entries.question_text: What kind of man is quite the opposite type of ‘supercilious’?
entries.options_raw: (a) Affable (b) Haughty (c) Disdainful (d) Wicked
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Supercilious' means arrogant and behaving as if one is superior to others. 'Affable' means friendly, good-natured, and easy to talk to, which is the direct opposite.

entries.question_text: How many eggs have your hens___this month? -Which is the following words best completes the above sentence?
entries.options_raw: (a) lain (b) laid (c) lay (d) lied
entries.explanation: Explanation: The sentence is in the present perfect tense (have + past participle). The verb required is 'to lay' (to produce an egg). Its past participle is 'laid'. 'Lain' is the past participle of 'to lie' (to recline).

entries.question_text: The walls of our house have been painted_____green. -Which is the correct preposition in the blank above?
entries.options_raw: (a) no preposition (b) by (c) in (d) with
entries.explanation: Explanation: When a color is used as a direct object complement to describe the result of an action like painting, no preposition is needed. The structure is "paint something [color]".

entries.question_text: Can you tell me where____? Which of the following is the best clause in the above sentence?
entries.options_raw: (a) does Mr. Ali live (b) Mr. Alive does live (c) Mr. Ali lives (d) lives Mr. Ali
entries.explanation: Explanation: This is an embedded question within a larger sentence. In such cases, the clause follows a standard statement word order (Subject + Verb), not the inverted question order (Auxiliary + Subject + Verb). So, "where Mr. Ali lives" is correct.

entries.question_text: What is the full name of the great American short story writer O’Henry?
entries.options_raw: (a) Walt Whitman (b) William Sydney Porter (c) Marjorie Kinnan Rawlings (d) Mark Twain
entries.explanation: Explanation: O. Henry was the pen name of the American short story writer William Sydney Porter.

entries.question_text: Now-a-days many villages are lit______electricity. – Which is the correct preposition in the above blank?
entries.options_raw: (a) with (b) by (c) from (d) on
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'By' is used to show the means or agent of an action. The villages are lit 'by means of' electricity. While 'with' can sometimes indicate a tool, 'by' is more appropriate for an abstract means like electricity.

entries.question_text: The second anniversary celebration of our college will be held on December 15.- Which of the following is the correct phrase for ‘will be held’ above?
entries.options_raw: (a) takes off (b) comes off (c) will bring about (d) will come round
entries.explanation: Explanation: The phrasal verb 'to come off' means to take place or to happen as planned. It is a suitable synonym for 'will be held' in this context.

entries.question_text: Dog days means-

options.label: b
options.text: a period of having youthful flings

entries.options_raw: (a) a period of being carefree (b) a period of having youthful flings (c) a period of misfortune (d) hot weather
entries.explanation: Explanation: The term 'dog days' refers to the hottest, most sultry period of summer, typically in July and August in the Northern Hemisphere.

entries.question_text: The speaker failed to make the audience ______ to him patiently. – Which of the following is the correct verb form in the blank above
entries.options_raw: (a) to listen (b) listening (c) listened (d) listen
entries.explanation: Explanation: The verb 'make' in its causative form (make someone do something) is followed by the bare infinitive (the base form of the verb without 'to'). Therefore, 'listen' is the correct form. The structure is: make + object + base verb.

entries.question_text: Which of the following ages in literary history is the latest?
entries.options_raw: (a) The Augustan Age (b) The Victorian Age (c) The Georgian Age (d) The Restoration Age
entries.explanation: Explanation: The chronological order of these literary ages is: The Restoration Age (1660-1700), The Augustan Age (1700-1745), The Victorian Age (1837-1901), and The Georgian Age (1910-1936). Therefore, the Georgian Age is the latest among the given options.

entries.question_text: The first English dictionary was compiled by-
entries.options_raw: (a) Iazak Walton (b) Samuel Johnson (c) Samuel Butler (d) Sir Thomas Browne
entries.explanation: Explanation: Samuel Johnson, a prominent English writer, compiled 'A Dictionary of the English Language', which was published in 1755. It is considered one of the most influential dictionaries in the history of the English language.

entries.question_text: My uncle has three sons, ____ work in the same office. Which of the following is the best form of pronoun in the above sentence?
entries.options_raw: (a) All of them (b) Who all (c) they all (d) All of whom
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'All of whom' is the correct choice as it acts as a non-restrictive relative clause connecting the two ideas. 'Whom' is the object of the preposition 'of' and refers back to the 'three sons'. Using 'All of them' would create a run-on sentence.

entries.question_text: People always remember patriots. Which of the following is the best passive form of the above sentence?

options.label: a
options.text: The patriots will always be remembered by people

options.label: b
options.text: The patriots are always being remembered

options.label: c
options.text: People are always remembered by The patriots

entries.options_raw: (a) The patriots will always be remembered by people (b) The patriots are always being remembered (c) People are always remembered by The patriots (d) The patriots are always remembered
entries.explanation: Explanation: The original sentence is in the simple present tense (remember). The passive form for this tense is 'am/is/are + past participle'. The object 'patriots' becomes the subject. Since 'by people' is understood and often omitted in passive voice, 'The patriots are always remembered' is the most concise and correct passive form.

entries.question_text: What is the meaning of the word ‘intrepid’?
entries.options_raw: (a) arrogant (b) belligerent (c) questioning (d) fearless
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Intrepid' means resolutely fearless or dauntless. It describes someone who is very brave and not afraid of danger or difficulties.

entries.question_text: What is the meaning of the expression ‘bottom line’?

options.label: c
options.text: The last line of a book

entries.options_raw: (a) The final step (b) The end of a road (c) The last line of a book (d) The essential point
entries.explanation: Explanation: The idiom 'the bottom line' refers to the most important fact in a situation, the fundamental and crucial point. It can also refer to the final profit or loss of a business.

entries.question_text: The word ‘plurality’ means-

options.label: d
options.text: The holding of more than one office at a time

entries.options_raw: (a) The letter ‘S’ (b) Men and women (c) Chaos and confusion (d) The holding of more than one office at a time
entries.correct_answer: (d) The holding of more than one office at a time
entries.explanation: Explanation: While 'plurality' can mean the state of being plural, it has a specific meaning in a political or ecclesiastical context: the holding of more than one office or position (like a benefice) by one person at the same time.

entries.question_text: ‘Pediatric’ relates to the treatment of –
entries.options_raw: (a) Adults (b) Children (c) Old people (d) Women
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Pediatrics' is the branch of medicine dealing with the health and medical care of infants, children, and adolescents. Thus, 'pediatric' relates to the treatment of children.

entries.question_text: ‘Boot leg’ means to-
entries.options_raw: (a) distribute (b) export (c) import (d) smuggle
entries.explanation: Explanation: The term 'bootleg' means to make, distribute, or sell goods, especially alcohol or recordings, illegally. This is synonymous with smuggling.

entries.question_text: Are you doing anything special ____ the weekend? -fill in the gap with appropriate preposition.
entries.options_raw: (a) in (b) for (c) on (d) at
entries.explanation: Explanation: In British English, 'at the weekend' is standard. In American English, 'on the weekend' is more common. Since both are used, 'at' is a perfectly correct answer, often preferred in formal contexts.

entries.question_text: Which of the following is a correct sentence?

options.label: a
options.text: He was too clever not to miss the point

options.label: b
options.text: He was to clever to miss the point

options.label: c
options.text: He was too clever to miss the point

options.label: d
options.text: He was too clever to grasp the point

entries.options_raw: (a) He was too clever not to miss the point (b) He was to clever to miss the point (c) He was too clever to miss the point (d) He was too clever to grasp the point
entries.correct_answer: (c) He was too clever to miss the point
entries.explanation: Explanation: The structure 'too + adjective + to + verb' has a negative implication. 'He was too clever to miss the point' means he was so clever that he would not miss the point. This sentence is grammatically correct and makes logical sense. Option (a) is a double negative and confusing. Option (b) misspells 'too'. Option (d) contradicts the meaning of 'clever'.

entries.question_text: The ‘Poet Laureate’ is-

options.label: a
options.text: the best poet of the country

options.label: b
options.text: a winner of the Noble Prize in poetry

entries.options_raw: (a) the best poet of the country (b) a winner of the Noble Prize in poetry (c) the Court Poet of England (d) a classical poet
entries.explanation: Explanation: The Poet Laureate is an honorary position appointed by the monarch of the United Kingdom, currently on the advice of the Prime Minister. The appointee is traditionally expected to write verses for significant national occasions. It is essentially the official court poet.

entries.question_text: Which of the following school of literary writings is connected with a medical theory?
entries.options_raw: (a) Comedy of Manners (b) Theater of the Absurd (c) Heroic Tragedy (d) Comedy of Humours
entries.explanation: Explanation: The Comedy of Humours is a genre of dramatic comedy that focuses on a character or range of characters, each of whom exhibits two or more overriding 'humours' that dominate their personality. This concept is based on the ancient Greek medical theory of the four humours (blood, phlegm, yellow bile, black bile), which were believed to determine a person's temperament.

entries.question_text: Who of the following was both a poet and painter?
entries.options_raw: (a) Keats (b) Donne (c) Blake (d) Spenser
entries.explanation: Explanation: William Blake was a seminal figure in the history of the poetry and visual arts of the Romantic Age. He was a master poet, painter, and printmaker. Many of his famous books of poetry, like 'Songs of Innocence and of Experience', were self-illustrated.

entries.question_text: What is the synonym of ‘incredible’?
entries.options_raw: (a) Unbelievable (b) Unthinkable (c) Unlikely (d) Unthinking
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Incredible' means difficult or impossible to believe. Its most direct synonym is 'Unbelievable'.

entries.question_text: What is the antonym of ‘famous’?
entries.options_raw: (a) Opaque (b) illiterate (c) Obscure (d) Immature
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Famous' means known about by many people. The antonym is 'obscure', which means not known to many people, unimportant and insignificant.

entries.question_text: ‘Plebiscite’ is a term related to –
entries.options_raw: (a) Medicine (b) Technology (c) Law (d) Politics
entries.explanation: Explanation: A plebiscite is a direct vote by the entire electorate of a state or country on some important public question, such as a change in the constitution or a choice of sovereignty. It is a tool of direct democracy and is therefore related to politics.

entries.question_text: Who wrote ‘beauty is truth, truth beauty’?
entries.options_raw: (a) Shakespeare (b) Wordsworth (c) Keats (d) Eliot
entries.explanation: Explanation: This famous line is from the poem 'Ode on a Grecian Urn' by the English Romantic poet John Keats. The full line is "'Beauty is truth, truth beauty,' – that is all / Ye know on earth, and all ye need to know."

entries.question_text: Many islands make up-
entries.options_raw: (a) an isles (b) an archipelago (c) a peninsula (d) a continent
entries.explanation: Explanation: An archipelago is a chain, cluster, or collection of islands, or sometimes a sea containing a small number of scattered islands.

entries.question_text: The word ‘imbibe’ means :
entries.options_raw: (a) to learn (b) To tinge (c) To drink (d) To acquire
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'To imbibe' literally means to drink, especially alcohol. It can also be used metaphorically to mean to absorb or assimilate ideas or knowledge.

entries.question_text: The word ‘homogeneous’ means:
entries.options_raw: (a) Of the same kind (b) Of the same place (c) Of the same race (d) Of the same density
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Homogeneous' is an adjective that describes something as consisting of parts or elements that are all of the same kind or nature.

entries.question_text: The synonym of ‘genesis’ is-
entries.options_raw: (a) introduction (b) preface (c) beginning (d) foreword
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Genesis' means the origin or the mode of formation of something. 'Beginning' is the closest synonym, as it also refers to the start or origin.

entries.question_text: The word ‘ecological’ is related to-
entries.options_raw: (a) Atmosphere (b) Pollution (c) Environment (d) Demography
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Ecological' relates to ecology, which is the scientific study of the relations that living organisms have with respect to each other and their natural environment.

entries.question_text: Which of the following sentence is correct?

options.label: a
options.text: One of my friends are a lawyer

options.label: b
options.text: One of my friends is a lawyer

options.label: c
options.text: One of my friend is a lawyer

options.label: d
options.text: One of my friends are lawyers

entries.options_raw: (a) One of my friends are a lawyer (b) One of my friends is a lawyer (c) One of my friend is a lawyer (d) One of my friends are lawyers
entries.correct_answer: (b) One of my friends is a lawyer
entries.explanation: Explanation: The phrase 'one of' is followed by a plural noun ('friends') but takes a singular verb ('is') because the subject is 'one'.

entries.question_text: The correct passive of ”Sheila was writing a letter” is –

options.label: a
options.text: A letter was written by Sheila

options.label: b
options.text: A letter was being writing by Sheila

options.label: c
options.text: A letter was being written by Sheila

options.label: d
options.text: A letter was been written by sheila

entries.options_raw: (a) A letter was written by Sheila (b) A letter was being writing by Sheila (c) A letter was being written by Sheila (d) A letter was been written by sheila
entries.correct_answer: (c) A letter was being written by Sheila
entries.explanation: Explanation: The sentence is in the Past Continuous tense (was + verb-ing). Its passive form is was/were + being + past participle of the verb (written).

entries.question_text: Which of the following sentences is correct?

options.label: a
options.text: That shirt which he bought is blue in colour

options.label: b
options.text: The shirt that which he bought is blue in colour

options.label: c
options.text: Which shirt he bought is blue in colour

options.label: d
options.text: The shirt which he bought is blue in colour

entries.options_raw: (a) That shirt which he bought is blue in colour (b) The shirt that which he bought is blue in colour (c) Which shirt he bought is blue in colour (d) The shirt which he bought is blue in colour
entries.correct_answer: (d) The shirt which he bought is blue in colour
entries.explanation: Explanation: This sentence correctly uses a defining relative clause 'which he bought' to specify which shirt is being discussed. The definite article 'The' is needed before 'shirt'.

entries.question_text: Which of the following sentence is a correct proverb?

options.label: a
options.text: Fools rush in where angels fear to tread

options.label: b
options.text: Fools rush in were an angels fears to tread

options.label: c
options.text: A fool rushes in where an angels fear to tread

options.label: d
options.text: Fools rush in where the angels fear to tread

entries.options_raw: (a) Fools rush in where angels fear to tread (b) Fools rush in were an angels fears to tread (c) A fool rushes in where an angels fear to tread (d) Fools rush in where the angels fear to tread
entries.correct_answer: (a) Fools rush in where angels fear to tread
entries.explanation: Explanation: This is a famous proverb from Alexander Pope's "An Essay on Criticism". It means that inexperienced or foolish people get involved in situations that more sensible people would avoid. The correct form uses plural 'fools' and 'angels' with corresponding verb forms 'rush' and 'fear'.

entries.question_text: In which century was the Victorian period?
entries.options_raw: (a) 17th century (b) 18th century (c) 19th century (d) 20th century
entries.explanation: Explanation: The Victorian period corresponds to the reign of Queen Victoria of Great Britain, from 1837 to 1901, which falls entirely within the 19th century.

entries.question_text: A person who writes about his own life writes-
entries.options_raw: (a) A chronicle (b) An autobiography (c) A diary (d) A biography
entries.explanation: Explanation: An autobiography is an account of a person's life written by that person. A biography is an account of someone's life written by someone else.

entries.question_text: Shakespeare is known mostly for his-
entries.options_raw: (a) Poetry (b) Novels (c) Autobiography (d) plays
entries.explanation: Explanation: While William Shakespeare also wrote famous sonnets (poetry), he is most renowned worldwide for his plays, such as 'Hamlet', 'Macbeth', and 'Romeo and Juliet'.

entries.question_text: A pilgrim is a person who undertakes a journey to a-
entries.options_raw: (a) Holy place (b) A mosque (c) A bazar (d) A new country
entries.explanation: Explanation: A pilgrim is a person who journeys to a sacred or holy place for religious reasons. A mosque is one type of holy place, but 'Holy place' is the general and most appropriate term.

entries.question_text: Something which is obnoxious means that it is-
entries.options_raw: (a) Very dangerous (b) Very pleasant (c) Very ugly (d) Very unpleasant
entries.explanation: Explanation: The word 'obnoxious' means extremely unpleasant, offensive, or hateful.

entries.question_text: Something that is ‘fresh’ is something-
entries.options_raw: (a) Recently printed of published (b) In fairly good condition (c) Disrespectful (d) Pleasant
entries.explanation: Explanation: While 'fresh' can mean recently made or new, in a general context (like 'fresh produce' or 'a fresh coat of paint'), it implies being in a good, not spoiled or stale, condition. Option (b) is the most general and fitting description among the choices.

entries.question_text: A fantasy is-
entries.options_raw: (a) An imaginary story (b) A funny film (c) A history (d) A real life event
entries.explanation: Explanation: A fantasy is a genre of fiction that typically features magic, supernatural elements, and imaginary worlds. Therefore, it is an imaginary story.

entries.question_text: An ordinance is-
entries.options_raw: (a) A book (b) An arms factory (c) A news paper journal (d) A law
entries.explanation: Explanation: An ordinance is an authoritative order or decree. In a governmental context, it is a piece of legislation enacted by a municipal authority or a special decree promulgated by a head of state, which has the force of law.

entries.question_text: Three score is –
entries.options_raw: (a) Thirty times (b) Three hundred times (c) Three times twenty (d) More than three
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Score' is an old term for the number 20. Therefore, 'three score' means 3 times 20, which equals 60.

entries.question_text: The antonym of ‘indifference’ is –
entries.options_raw: (a) Ardour (b) Compassion (c) Anxiety (d) Concern
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Indifference' means a lack of interest, concern, or sympathy. Its opposite would be the presence of these feelings. 'Concern' (care, interest) is the most direct antonym. 'Ardour' (passion) and 'compassion' (sympathy) are also opposites but 'concern' is a broader and better fit.

entries.question_text: The sentence with correct punctuations-

options.label: ক
options.text: Maria, my student, is on leave to-day.

options.label: খ
options.text: Maria my student, is on leave to-day.

options.label: গ
options.text: Maria my student is on leave to-day.

options.label: ঘ
options.text: Maria my student is, on leave to-day.

entries.options_raw: ক) Maria, my student, is on leave to-day. খ) Maria my student, is on leave to-day. গ) Maria my student is on leave to-day. ঘ) Maria my student is, on leave to-day.
entries.correct_answer: ক) Maria, my student, is on leave to-day.
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'my student' is an appositive, a phrase that renames the noun 'Maria'. An appositive phrase should be set off by commas. Therefore, commas are needed before 'my' and after 'student'.

entries.question_text: The antonym for ‘Inimical’-
entries.options_raw: ক) Hostile খ) Friendly গ) Indifferent ঘ) Angry
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Inimical' means hostile or unfriendly. Its direct antonym (opposite) is 'Friendly'.

entries.question_text: The synonym for ‘efface’-
entries.options_raw: ক) Improve খ) Exhaust গ) Rub out ঘ) Cut out
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Efface' means to erase a mark from a surface or to make oneself appear insignificant. 'Rub out' is the closest synonym, meaning to erase or remove.

entries.question_text: The best passive form of the sentence: ‘We don’t like idle people’-

options.label: ক
options.text: We are not liked by idle people.

options.label: খ
options.text: Idle people are not like us.

options.label: গ
options.text: Idle people are not liked by us.

options.label: ঘ
options.text: Idle people are not of our liking.

entries.options_raw: ক) We are not liked by idle people. খ) Idle people are not like us. গ) Idle people are not liked by us. ঘ) Idle people are not of our liking.
entries.correct_answer: গ) Idle people are not liked by us.
entries.explanation: Explanation: To make it passive, the object 'idle people' becomes the subject. The verb 'don't like' (Present Simple Negative) changes to 'are not liked'. The original subject 'We' becomes the object 'by us'.

entries.question_text: The correct sentence of the followings-

options.label: ক
options.text: The Nile is longest river in Africa.

options.label: খ
options.text: The Nile is Longest river in the Africa.

options.label: গ
options.text: Nile is longest river in Africa.

options.label: ঘ
options.text: The Nile is the longest river in Africa.

entries.options_raw: ক) The Nile is longest river in Africa. খ) The Nile is Longest river in the Africa. গ) Nile is longest river in Africa. ঘ) The Nile is the longest river in Africa.
entries.correct_answer: ঘ) The Nile is the longest river in Africa.
entries.explanation: Explanation: The definite article 'the' is used before the names of rivers (The Nile) and before superlative adjectives (the longest). 'Africa' is a proper noun (continent) and generally does not take an article.

entries.question_text: Browning was the composer of any of the following poems-
entries.options_raw: ক) Two voices খ) The Scholar Gipsy গ) Andreadel Sarto ঘ) Oneone
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Andrea del Sarto' is a famous dramatic monologue by the Victorian poet Robert Browning. 'The Scholar Gipsy' is by Matthew Arnold and 'Two Voices' is by Tennyson.

entries.question_text: The right word to fill in the gap of the following sentence- ‘Give her a telephone number to ring ____ she gets lost’-
entries.options_raw: ক) whether খ) in case গ) unless ঘ) perhaps
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'in case' is used to talk about things we should do as a precaution against a possible future situation. Here, the precaution is giving a telephone number.

entries.question_text: The synonym of ‘Franchise’ –
entries.options_raw: ক) Privilege খ) Utility গ) French ঘ) Frankness
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Franchise' most commonly refers to the right to vote. More broadly, it means a special right or privilege granted to a person or group, especially by a government.

entries.question_text: The opposite word of ‘sluggish’-
entries.options_raw: ক) Animated খ) Dull গ) Heavy ঘ) Slow
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Sluggish' means slow-moving or inactive. 'Animated' means full of life and excitement, which is the best opposite. 'Dull', 'Heavy', and 'Slow' are synonyms or related to 'sluggish'.

entries.question_text: The correct spelling is-
entries.options_raw: ক) Humourous খ) Humourious গ) Humorous ঘ) Humorious
entries.explanation: Explanation: The correct spelling for the adjective meaning 'causing amusement' is H-U-M-O-R-O-U-S.

entries.question_text: ‘Equivocation’ means-

options.label: খ
options.text: Equal opportunity to get a job

options.label: ঘ
options.text: Two contrary things in the same statement

entries.options_raw: ক) A true statement খ) Equal opportunity to get a job গ) Free expression of opinions ঘ) Two contrary things in the same statement
entries.correct_answer: ঘ) Two contrary things in the same statement
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Equivocation' is the use of ambiguous language to conceal the truth or to avoid committing oneself. It often involves saying something that can be interpreted in two contradictory ways.

entries.question_text: When a person says he’s all in’, it means-
entries.options_raw: ক) he is very tired খ) He has arrived গ) He has finished packing ঘ) he has got everything
entries.explanation: Explanation: The idiom 'all in' is an informal way of saying one is completely exhausted or very tired.

entries.question_text: ‘Bill of fare’ is-

options.label: ঘ
options.text: A list of dishes at a restaurant

entries.options_raw: ক) a chart of bus fare খ) A price list গ) A valuable document ঘ) A list of dishes at a restaurant
entries.correct_answer: ঘ) A list of dishes at a restaurant
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Bill of fare' is a synonym for 'menu'. It is a list of the food items available at a restaurant.

entries.question_text: A ‘bull market’ means that share prices are-
entries.options_raw: ক) Falling খ) Rising গ) Moving ঘ) Static
entries.explanation: Explanation: In finance, a 'bull market' is a condition of a financial market in which prices are rising or are expected to rise. The opposite is a 'bear market', where prices are falling.

entries.question_text: ‘Blue chips’ are-

options.label: খ
options.text: Industrial shares considered to be a safe investment

options.label: গ
options.text: Industrial shares considered to be a risky investment

options.label: ঘ
options.text: A list of dishes at a restaurant

entries.options_raw: ক) Securities issued by the government খ) Industrial shares considered to be a safe investment গ) Industrial shares considered to be a risky investment ঘ) A list of dishes at a restaurant
entries.correct_answer: খ) Industrial shares considered to be a safe investment
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Blue chip' stocks are shares of large, well-established, and financially sound companies that have operated for many years and are considered a reliable and safe investment.

entries.question_text: ‘Razzmatazz’ means-
entries.options_raw: ক) A musical instrument খ) A well-planned programme গ) A noisy activity ঘ) A musical drama
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Razzmatazz' refers to noisy and exciting activity or display designed to attract attention.

entries.question_text: ‘Blockbuster’ means-

options.label: ক
options.text: A large solid piece of store

options.label: খ
options.text: A device to cut off a person’s head as a punishment

options.label: ঘ
options.text: A powerful explosive to demolish buildings

entries.options_raw: ক) A large solid piece of store খ) A device to cut off a person’s head as a punishment গ) Something that makes movement difficult ঘ) A powerful explosive to demolish buildings
entries.correct_answer: ঘ) A powerful explosive to demolish buildings
entries.explanation: Explanation: Historically, a 'blockbuster' was a large, powerful bomb capable of destroying an entire city block. In modern usage, it more commonly refers to a very successful movie or book, but the original meaning is related to demolition.

entries.question_text: Any one of the following pairs are literary collaborators-
entries.options_raw: ক) Eliot and Pound খ) Yeats and Eliot গ) Pope and Dryden ঘ) Shelly and Keats
entries.explanation: Explanation: Ezra Pound was a crucial figure in the development of T.S. Eliot's poetry. Pound famously edited Eliot's landmark poem 'The Waste Land', making them significant literary collaborators.

entries.question_text: ‘To read between the lines’ means-

options.label: গ
options.text: To read quickly to save time

options.label: ঘ
options.text: To read carefully to find out any hidden meaning

entries.options_raw: ক) To read carefully খ) To read only some lines গ) To read quickly to save time ঘ) To read carefully to find out any hidden meaning
entries.correct_answer: ঘ) To read carefully to find out any hidden meaning
entries.explanation: Explanation: This idiom means to understand the real or hidden meaning behind what is explicitly said or written.

entries.question_text: The last word of the proverb, ‘Handsome is that handsome__.’
entries.options_raw: ক) works খ) thinks গ) says ঘ) does
entries.explanation: Explanation: The complete proverb is "Handsome is as handsome does," which means that a person's actions (what they do) are more important than their physical appearance in determining their true character.

entries.question_text: Many companies now have employee assistance programs that enable employees, free of charge, to improve their physical fitness, reduce stress, and learn ways to stop smoking. These programs increase worker productivity, reduce absenteeism and lessen insurance costs for employee health care. Therefore, these programs benefit the company as well as the employee. ____ Which of the following, if true, most significantly strengthens the conclusion above?

options.label: ক
options.text: Physical fitness programs are often the most popular services offered to employees.

options.label: খ
options.text: Studies have shown that training in stress management is not effective for many people.

options.label: গ
options.text: Regular exercise reduces people’s risk of heart disease and provides them with increased energy

options.label: ঘ
options.text: Employee assistance programs require companies to hire people to supervise the various programs offered.

entries.options_raw:
(ক) Physical fitness programs are often the most popular services offered to employees.
 
(খ) Studies have shown that training in stress management is not effective for many people.
 
(গ) Regular exercise reduces people’s risk of heart disease and provides them with increased energy
 
(ঘ) Employee assistance programs require companies to hire people to supervise the various programs offered.
entries.correct_answer: (ক) Physical fitness programs are often the most popular services offered to employees.
entries.explanation: অনুচ্ছেদের উপসংহার হলো এই প্রোগ্রামগুলো কোম্পানি এবং কর্মচারী উভয়েরই উপকার করে। যদি শারীরিক সুস্থতা প্রোগ্রামগুলো কর্মচারীদের মধ্যে সবচেয়ে জনপ্রিয় সেবা হয়, তার মানে হলো কর্মচারীরা এই প্রোগ্রামগুলো ব্যাপকভাবে ব্যবহার করে। এর ফলে উৎপাদনশীলতা বৃদ্ধি এবং অনুপস্থিতি হ্রাসের মতো সুবিধাগুলো অর্জিত হওয়ার সম্ভাবনা বাড়ে, যা কোম্পানির জন্য উপকারী। তাই এই তথ্যটি উপসংহারকে শক্তিশালী করে।

entries.question_text: Choose the answer that is closest in meaning to the following sentence: ”Despite the great difference in size, shape and function, all human cells have the same 46 chromosomes.”

options.label: ক
options.text: All human cells are the same because the 46 chromosomes govern size, shape and function.

options.label: খ
options.text: Difference in size, shape and function are not very great because all human cells have the same 46 chromosomes.

options.label: গ
options.text: The size, shape and function of human cells are the same, but the 46 chromosomes are different.

options.label: ঘ
options.text: Although the 46 chromosomes are the same in all human cells, there are difference in the size, shape and function.

entries.options_raw:
(ক) All human cells are the same because the 46 chromosomes govern size, shape and function.
 
(খ) Difference in size, shape and function are not very great because all human cells have the same 46 chromosomes.
 
(গ) The size, shape and function of human cells are the same, but the 46 chromosomes are different.
 
(ঘ) Although the 46 chromosomes are the same in all human cells, there are difference in the size, shape and function.
entries.correct_answer: (ঘ) Although the 46 chromosomes are the same in all human cells, there are difference in the size, shape and function.
entries.explanation: প্রদত্ত বাক্যের অর্থ হলো - "আকার, আকৃতি এবং কাজের বিশাল পার্থক্য থাকা সত্ত্বেও, সমস্ত মানব কোষে একই ৪৬টি ক্রোমোজোম রয়েছে।" বিকল্প (ঘ) এর অর্থ হলো - "যদিও সমস্ত মানব কোষে ৪৬টি ক্রোমোজোম একই, তবুও আকার, আকৃতি এবং কাজে পার্থক্য রয়েছে।" 'Despite' এবং 'Although' উভয়ই বৈপরীত্য প্রকাশ করে, তাই বাক্য দুটির অর্থ একই।

entries.question_text:
In the following four questions, choose the word or phrase that is most nearly similar or opposite in meaning to the word given in the question:-
INFRINGE
entries.options_raw: (ক) Transgress (খ) Purloin (গ) Invade (ঘ) Intrude
entries.explanation: Infringe অর্থ আইন বা নিয়ম লঙ্ঘন করা, সীমানা অতিক্রম করা। Transgress শব্দের অর্থও আইন বা সীমা লঙ্ঘন করা। তাই এ দুটি শব্দ সমার্থক (similar)।

entries.question_text: BROCHURE
entries.options_raw: (ক) Opening (খ) Pamphlet (গ) Bureau (ঘ) Censor
entries.explanation: Brochure হলো একটি ছোট বই বা ম্যাগাজিন যাতে কোনো পণ্য বা পরিষেবা সম্পর্কে ছবি ও তথ্য থাকে। Pamphlet হলো একটি ছোট পুস্তিকা বা লিফলেট যাতে একটি নির্দিষ্ট বিষয় সম্পর্কে তথ্য থাকে। শব্দ দুটি প্রায় সমার্থক।

entries.question_text: EQUIVOCAL
entries.options_raw: (ক) Universal (খ) Mistaken (গ) Quaint (ঘ) Clear
entries.explanation: Equivocal শব্দের অর্থ দ্ব্যর্থক, অস্পষ্ট বা সন্দেহজনক। প্রশ্নে similar or opposite উভয়ই হতে পারে। Clear শব্দের অর্থ পরিষ্কার বা স্পষ্ট, যা Equivocal এর বিপরীত (opposite)।

entries.question_text: ILLUSIVE
entries.options_raw: (ক) Not deceptive (খ) Not certain (গ) Not obvious (ঘ) Not coherent
entries.explanation: Illusive শব্দের অর্থ অলীক, মায়াময় বা প্রতারণামূলক (deceptive)। প্রশ্নে similar or opposite উভয়ই হতে পারে। Not deceptive (অপ্রতারণামূলক) হলো Illusive এর বিপরীত (opposite) অর্থ।

entries.question_text: In the following three questions, a related pair of words is followed by four pairs of word. Select the pair that best expresses a relationship similar to the expressed in the original pair: CARPENTER : SAW
entries.options_raw: (ক) Stenographer : typewriter (খ) Painter : brush (গ) Lawyer : brief (ঘ) Seamstress : scissors
entries.explanation: সম্পর্কটি হলো কর্মী এবং তার প্রধান কাটার যন্ত্র (worker and his cutting tool)। Carpenter (সূত্রধর) কাঠ কাটার জন্য Saw (করাত) ব্যবহার করে। একইভাবে, Seamstress (দর্জি) কাপড় কাটার জন্য Scissors (কাঁচি) ব্যবহার করে। Painter তুলি ব্যবহার করে আঁকার জন্য, কাটার জন্য নয়।

entries.question_text: FIRE : ASHES
entries.options_raw: (ক) Accident : delay (খ) Water : waves (গ) Event : memories (ঘ) Wood : splinters
entries.explanation: Fire (আগুন) লাগার পর যা অবশিষ্ট থাকে তা হলো Ashes (ছাই)। এটি একটি ঘটনা ও তার পরিণতির সম্পর্ক। একইভাবে, কোনো Event (ঘটনা) ঘটে যাওয়ার পর যা অবশিষ্ট থাকে তা হলো Memories (স্মৃতি)।

entries.question_text: STARE : GLANCE
entries.options_raw: (ক) gulp : sip (খ) confide : tell (গ) scorn : admire (ঘ) participate : observe
entries.explanation: সম্পর্কটি তীব্রতা বা পরিমাণের। Stare হলো একদৃষ্টে দীর্ঘক্ষণ তাকিয়ে থাকা, আর Glance হলো দ্রুত একবার তাকানো। একইভাবে, Gulp হলো দ্রুত ও বড় ঢোক গিলে পান করা, আর Sip হলো অল্প পরিমাণে ধীরে ধীরে পান করা।

entries.question_text:
Each sentence below has two blanks. Choose the set of words for each blank that best fits the meaning of the sentence as a whole:
Although a few years ago the fundamental fact about the milky way seemed fairly well _____ now even its mass and radius have come into ______.
entries.options_raw: (ক) determined — resolution (খ) established — question (গ) ignored — danger (ঘ) diminished — disrepute
entries.explanation: 'Although' এবং 'now' দ্বারা বাক্যে একটি বৈপরীত্য বোঝানো হচ্ছে। অতীতে মিল্কিওয়ে সম্পর্কে তথ্যগুলো সুপ্রতিষ্ঠিত (established) ছিল, কিন্তু এখন সেগুলো প্রশ্নের (question) সম্মুখীন হয়েছে। এই জুটিই বাক্যের অর্থকে সম্পূর্ণ করে।

entries.question_text: Because she had reputation for ___ we were surprised and pleased when she greeted us so____.
entries.options_raw: (ক) insolence–irately (খ) insouciance–cordially (গ) arrogance–disdainfully (ঘ) querulousness–affably
entries.explanation: বাক্যটিতে বলা হচ্ছে যে আমরা তার অভ্যর্থনা পেয়ে 'অবাক এবং খুশি' হয়েছিলাম, যা ইঙ্গিত দেয় যে তার অভ্যর্থনাটি বন্ধুত্বপূর্ণ ছিল এবং তার খ্যাতি ছিল এর বিপরীত। 'Affably' (অমায়িকভাবে) একটি বন্ধুত্বপূর্ণ অভ্যর্থনা। এর বিপরীত খ্যাতি হলো 'querulousness' (খিটখিটে বা ঝগড়াটে স্বভাব)।

entries.question_text: A ____ statement is an ____ comparison; it does not compare. Things explicitly but suggest a likeness between them.
entries.options_raw: (ক) sarcastic — unfair (খ) metaphorical — implied (গ) sanguine — inherent (ঘ) blatant — overt
entries.explanation: যে বাক্য স্পষ্টভাবে তুলনা না করে সাদৃশ্য নির্দেশ করে তাকে রূপক বা metaphorical statement বলে। এই ধরনের তুলনা সরাসরি বলা হয় না, বরং উহ্য বা implied থাকে। সুতরাং, 'metaphorical' এবং 'implied' শব্দ দুটি সঠিক।

entries.question_text:
Choose the word or phrase that best fill the blank space to complete the sentences:
If a ruby is heated it ___ temporarily lose its color.
entries.options_raw: (ক) would (খ) will (গ) does (ঘ) Has
entries.explanation: এটি একটি First Conditional বা Zero Conditional বাক্য যা একটি বৈজ্ঞানিক সত্য প্রকাশ করছে। ഇത്തരം ক্ষেত্রে if-clause-এ Present Indefinite Tense এবং main clause-এ Future Indefinite Tense (will + verb) ব্যবহৃত হয়।

entries.question_text: All of the people at the AAME conference are—
entries.options_raw: (ক) Mathematic teachers (খ) Mathematics teachers (গ) Mathematics teacher (ঘ) Mathematic’s teachers
entries.explanation: এখানে 'Mathematics' (গণিত) শব্দটি একটি noun যা 'teachers' (বিশেষ্য) শব্দটিকে modify করার জন্য adjective হিসেবে কাজ করছে। এই ধরনের compound noun-এ প্রথম noun-টি সাধারণত singular থাকে। Mathematics本身 একটি 's' যুক্ত শব্দ। তাই সঠিক রূপটি হলো 'Mathematics teachers'।

entries.question_text: Prices for bicycles can run ____ TK. 2,000.00.
entries.options_raw: (ক) as high as (খ) so high as (গ) as high to (ঘ) as high for
entries.explanation: কোনো কিছুর সর্বোচ্চ সীমা বা পরিমাণ বোঝাতে 'as high as' phrase-টি ব্যবহৃত হয়। এর অর্থ "সর্বোচ্চ এত পর্যন্ত"।

entries.question_text: Travellers ____ their reservations well in advance if they want to fly during the Eid holidays.
entries.options_raw: (ক) had better to get (খ) had to get better (গ) had better get (ঘ) had better got
entries.explanation: 'Had better' একটি semi-modal verb যা পরামর্শ বা সুপারিশ দেওয়ার জন্য ব্যবহৃত হয়। এর পরে সর্বদা verb-এর base form (get) বসে, 'to' বসে না।

entries.question_text: A seventeen year old is not — to vote in an election.
entries.options_raw: (ক) old enough (খ) as old enough (গ) enough old (ঘ) enough old as
entries.explanation: Adjective বা adverb-এর পরে 'enough' বসে। এখানে adjective হলো 'old'। সুতরাং সঠিক গঠনটি হলো 'old enough'।

entries.question_text: Almost everyone fails — on the first try.

options.label: গ
options.text: to have passed his driver’s test

entries.options_raw: (ক) in passing his driver’s test (খ) to his driver’s test (গ) to have passed his driver’s test (ঘ) passing his driver’s test
entries.explanation: 'Fail' verb-এর পর preposition 'in' এবং তারপর gerund (verb+ing) বসে। 'Fail in doing something' একটি সঠিক গঠন। তাই 'fails in passing' সঠিক উত্তর।

entries.question_text:
Throughout history, the search for salt has played an important role in society. Where it was scarce, salt was traded ounce for ounce with gold. Rome’s major highway was called the via salaria, that is the Salt Road. Along the road, Roman soldiers transported salt crystals from the salt flats at Ostia up the Tiber River. In return, they received a salarium or salary literally money paid to soldiers to buy salt. The old saying ”worth their salt” which to be valuable derives from the custom of payment during the Empire.
 
What does the passage mainly discuss?
entries.options_raw: (ক) The old saying (খ) The Roman Empire (গ) Salt (ঘ) Ancient Trade
entries.explanation: পুরো অনুচ্ছেদটি লবণ (Salt) নিয়ে আলোচনা করছে - এর ঐতিহাসিক গুরুত্ব, সোনার সাথে এর বাণিজ্য, রোমান সৈন্যদের বেতন হিসেবে এর ব্যবহার এবং এর থেকে উদ্ভূত প্রবাদ। তাই মূল আলোচ্য বিষয় হলো 'Salt'।

entries.question_text: According to the passage salt flats were located in-
entries.options_raw: (ক) Rome (খ) Tiber (গ) Ostia (ঘ) Salaria
entries.explanation: অনুচ্ছেদে স্পষ্টভাবে উল্লেখ আছে: "...Roman soldiers transported salt crystals from the salt flats at Ostia..."। অর্থাৎ, সল্ট ফ্ল্যাটগুলো ওস্টিয়াতে (Ostia) অবস্থিত ছিল।

entries.question_text: Salarium is a Latin word that means –
entries.options_raw: (ক) Salt (খ) Salary (গ) Soldiers (ঘ) the Salt Road
entries.explanation: অনুচ্ছেদে বলা হয়েছে: "In return, they received a salarium or salary..."। এটি সরাসরি 'salarium' শব্দটিকে 'salary' (বেতন) এর সাথে যুক্ত করে।

entries.question_text: If a man is,’worth his salt.’ he is-
entries.options_raw: (ক) a soldier (খ) a thirsty man (গ) A valuable employee (ঘ) a highly paid worker
entries.explanation: অনুচ্ছেদের শেষে বলা হয়েছে 'worth their salt' অর্থ 'to be valuable'। এই প্রবাদটি এমন একজন ব্যক্তিকে বোঝায় যিনি তার বেতনের যোগ্য, অর্থাৎ একজন মূল্যবান কর্মচারী (a valuable employee)।

entries.question_text: EXCITE : CALM –
entries.options_raw: (a) restrain : compose (b) agitate : trouble (c) upset : perturd (d) stimulate : cool down
entries.explanation: Explanation: Excite (উত্তেজিত করা) and Calm (শান্ত করা) are antonyms. Similarly, Stimulate (উদ্দীপ্ত করা) and Cool down (শান্ত হওয়া/করা) are antonyms, showing a cause and effect of quieting down.

entries.question_text: DELAY : EXPEDITE –
entries.options_raw: (a) related : halt (b) block : obstruct (c) drag : procrastinate (d) detain : dispatch
entries.explanation: Explanation: Delay (বিলম্ব করা) and Expedite (ত্বরান্বিত করা) are antonyms. Similarly, Detain (আটকে রাখা) and Dispatch (প্রেরণ করা) are opposite actions.

entries.question_text: ANARCHY : GOVERNMENT –
entries.options_raw: (a) penury : wealth (b) chaos : disorder (c) monarchy : republic (d) verbosity : words
entries.explanation: Explanation: Anarchy (নৈরাজ্য) is the absence of Government (সরকার). Similarly, Penury (চরম দারিদ্র্য) is the absence of Wealth (সম্পদ).

entries.question_text: VACCINE : PREVENT –
entries.options_raw: (a) wound : heal (b) victim : attend (c) antidote : counteract (d) diagnosis : cure
entries.explanation: Explanation: A Vaccine (টিকা) is used to prevent (প্রতিরোধ করা) disease. Similarly, an Antidote (প্রতিষেধক) is used to counteract (প্রতিরোধ করা) poison.

entries.question_text: ____ glass is, for all practical, a solid, its molecular structure is that of a liquid.
entries.options_raw: (a) Because (b) Since (c) Although (d) If
entries.explanation: Explanation: The sentence presents a contrast between two facts (it seems solid, but its structure is liquid-like). 'Although' is the correct conjunction to show this contrast.

entries.question_text: An intensive search was conducted by the detective to locate those criminals, who ______.
entries.options_raw: (a) have had escaped (b) had escaped (c) are escaping (d) have been escaping
entries.explanation: Explanation: The main clause is in the past tense ("was conducted"). The escaping of the criminals happened before the search. When two actions occur in the past, the earlier action takes the Past Perfect tense (had + V3). So, 'had escaped' is correct.

entries.question_text: The intellectual can no longer be said to live ____ the margins of society.
entries.options_raw: (a) against (b) beyond (c) inside (d) Before
entries.explanation: Explanation: "To live beyond the margins" means to live outside the conventional boundaries or mainstream of society. This phrase fits the context of an intellectual's position.

entries.question_text: According to the conditions of my scholarship, after finishing my degree ____.

options.label: a
options.text: my education will be employed by the University.

options.label: b
options.text: employment will be given to me by the University.

options.label: d
options.text: I will be employed of the University.

entries.options_raw: (a) my education will be employed by the University. (b) employment will be given to me by the University. (c) the University will employ me. (d) I will be employed of the University.
entries.explanation: Explanation: The introductory phrase "after finishing my degree" needs to modify the subject of the main clause. The person who finishes the degree is 'I', but 'I' is not the subject in options a, b, and d. Option (c) corrects this dangling modifier by making "the University" the subject, but it logically follows that after 'I' finish my degree, the university will employ 'me'. In the context of active vs passive voice, (c) is the most direct and clear statement.

entries.question_text: If a substance is cohesive, it tends to ____.
entries.options_raw: (a) retain heat (b) bend without much difficulty (c) stick together (d) break easily
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Cohesive' means characterized by or causing cohesion. Cohesion is the action or fact of forming a united whole, or the sticking together of particles of the same substance. Therefore, a cohesive substance tends to 'stick together'.

entries.question_text: He stopped his car ____ when the light turned red.
entries.options_raw: (a) abruptly (b) equitably (c) ambiguously (d) Incisively
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Abruptly' means suddenly and unexpectedly, which fits the context of stopping a car quickly when a traffic light turns red.

entries.question_text: The influence of the technological revolution in ____ and ____ the concentration of wealth and power in the hands of the few should worry us all.
entries.options_raw: (a) proliferating — diminishing (b) undermining — neutralizing (c) accelerating — intensifying (d) aggravating — demolishing
entries.explanation: Explanation: The sentence describes a negative influence. The technological revolution is likely to 'accelerate' (speed up) and 'intensify' (make stronger) the concentration of wealth and power, which is a cause for worry.
