entries.explanation: Explanation: A material noun is the name of a substance from which things are made. 'Mutton' (মেষশাবকের মাংস) is the name of a type of meat, hence a material noun.

entries.question_text: Reading is an excellent habit, Here, the ”Reading” word is a —–
entries.options_raw: (a) Verbal noun (b) Praticiple (c) Verb (d) Greund
entries.explanation: Explanation: When a verb ending in '-ing' is used as the subject of a sentence, it functions as a noun and is called a gerund.

entries.question_text: Which one of the following words is an example of a distributive pronoun?
entries.options_raw: (a) such (b) either (c) that (d) any
entries.explanation: Explanation: Distributive pronouns (each, either, neither) refer to persons or things one at a time.

entries.question_text: Who is not a Victorian poet?
entries.options_raw: (a) Mathew Arnold (b) Alexander Pope (c) Robert Browning (d) Alfred Tennyson
entries.explanation: Explanation: Matthew Arnold, Robert Browning, and Alfred Tennyson were prominent poets of the Victorian era (1837–1901). Alexander Pope was a leading poet of the Augustan Age (early 18th century).

entries.question_text: A speech of too many words is called—
entries.options_raw: (a) A big speech (b) Maiden speech (c) An unimportant speeech (d) A verbose speech
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Verbose' means using or expressed in more words than are needed. Therefore, a speech with too many words is a verbose speech.

entries.question_text: ”Strike while the iron is hot” is an example of —-
entries.options_raw: (a) Noun clause (b) Adjective clause (c) Adverbial clause (d) Subordinate clause
entries.explanation: Explanation: The clause 'while the iron is hot' modifies the verb 'strike' by indicating the time of the action. A clause that modifies a verb and indicates time is an adverbial clause of time.

entries.question_text: The play ”The Spanish Tragedy” is written by—-
entries.options_raw: (a) Thomas Kyd (b) Christopher Marlowe (c) Shakespeare (d) Ben Jonson
entries.explanation: Explanation: "The Spanish Tragedy" is an influential Elizabethan tragedy written by Thomas Kyd between 1582 and 1592. It established the genre of the revenge play.

entries.question_text: Who among the following Indian English writers is a famous novelist?
entries.options_raw: (a) Gayatri Chakravorty Spivak (b) R.K. Narayan (c) Nissim Ezekiel (d) Kamala Das
entries.explanation: Explanation: R.K. Narayan was a leading figure of early Indian literature in English, famous for his novels set in the fictional South Indian town of Malgudi. Nissim Ezekiel and Kamala Das were primarily poets, and Gayatri Spivak is a literary critic and theorist.

entries.question_text: The word ”Panegyric” means
entries.options_raw: (a) Criticism (b) elaborate praise (c) curse (d) high sound
entries.explanation: Explanation: A panegyric is a public speech or published text in praise of someone or something.

entries.question_text: Select the correctly spelt word :
entries.options_raw: (a) heterogeneous (b) hetarogeneous (c) hetrogeneous (d) hetroganeous
entries.explanation: Explanation: The correct spelling is 'heterogeneous', meaning diverse in character or content.

entries.question_text: Which period is known as ”The golden age of English literature ?
entries.options_raw: (a) The Victorian age (b) The Elizabethan age (c) The Restoration age (d) The Eighteenth Century
entries.explanation: Explanation: The Elizabethan Age (reign of Elizabeth I, 1558–1603) is often called the golden age of English literature due to the flourishing of poetry and drama, especially the works of Shakespeare.

entries.question_text: Which one is the correct indirect narration? ”Why have you beaten my dog?” he said to me.

options.label: a
options.text: He demanded me why had I beaten his dog

options.label: b
options.text: He asked me why I have had beaten his dog

options.label: c
options.text: He enquired me why had I had beaten his dog

options.label: d
options.text: He demanded of me why I had beaten his dog

entries.options_raw: (a) He demanded me why had I beaten his dog (b) He asked me why I have had beaten his dog (c) He enquired me why had I had beaten his dog (d) He demanded of me why I had beaten his dog
entries.correct_answer: (d) He demanded of me why I had beaten his dog
entries.explanation: Explanation: In indirect speech, an interrogative sentence becomes an assertive sentence. The reporting verb 'said' changes to 'asked' or 'demanded of'. The tense changes from present perfect to past perfect. The correct structure is 'He demanded of me why I had beaten his dog'.

entries.question_text: Who is the author of ”Man and Superman”?
entries.options_raw: (a) G.B. Shaw (b) Thomas Hardy (c) Ernest hemingway (d) Charles Dickens
entries.explanation: Explanation: "Man and Superman" is a four-act drama written by George Bernard Shaw in 1903.

entries.question_text: The most famous satirist in English literature is —
entries.options_raw: (a) Jonathan Swift (b) Alexander Popy (c) Joseph Addison (d) Richard Steel
entries.explanation: Explanation: Jonathan Swift is widely regarded as the foremost satirist in English literature, best known for works like "Gulliver's Travels" and "A Modest Proposal".

entries.question_text: Among is a preposition that is used when _____ people are involved.
entries.options_raw: (a) two (b) more than two (c) two or more than two (d) four only
entries.explanation: Explanation: Generally, 'between' is used for two people or things, while 'among' is used for more than two.

entries.question_text: The novelist has a hold of ____ in writing.
entries.options_raw: (a) manner (b) history (c) tradition (d) style
entries.explanation: Explanation: A novelist is distinguished by their unique 'style' of writing, which includes their choice of words, sentence structure, and narrative technique.

entries.question_text: A person who believes that laws and governments are not necessary is known as-
entries.options_raw: (a) a militant (b) an anarchist (c) a terrorist (d) an extremist
entries.explanation: Explanation: An anarchist is someone who believes in anarchism, a political philosophy that advocates self-governed societies based on voluntary institutions and rejects the state and all forms of compulsory government.

entries.question_text: He went to ______ hospital because he had ___ heart attack.
entries.options_raw: (a) no article, an (b) a, an (c) the, no article (d) no article, a
entries.explanation: Explanation: When referring to institutions like 'hospital', 'school', 'church' for their primary purpose (e.g., treatment, study), no article is used. 'Heart attack' is a singular countable noun here, and 'a' is used before it. So the correct form is: "He went to hospital because he had a heart attack."

entries.question_text: The word ‘florid’ indicates
entries.options_raw: (a) flour (b) foliage (c) floor (d) flower
entries.explanation: Explanation: The word 'florid' is etymologically related to the Latin word 'flos', meaning flower. 'Florid' can mean 'flowery in style' or 'having a red or flushed complexion', both of which draw a connection to flowers.

entries.question_text: Complete the following sentence : ‘Had I known you were waiting outside, I ___.

options.label: a
options.text: had invited you to come in

options.label: b
options.text: would invite you to come in

options.label: c
options.text: would be inviting you to come in

options.label: d
options.text: would have invited you to come in

entries.options_raw: (a) had invited you to come in (b) would invite you to come in (c) would be inviting you to come in (d) would have invited you to come in
entries.correct_answer: (d) would have invited you to come in
entries.explanation: Explanation: This is a third conditional sentence, used for unreal past conditions. The structure is: Had + subject + V3 (past participle), subject + would have + V3. Therefore, "would have invited" is the correct completion.

entries.question_text: A soporific speech is likely to ___.
entries.options_raw: (a) be incomprehensible (b) appeal primarily to emotions (c) put one to sleep (d) stimulate action
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Soporific' means tending to induce drowsiness or sleep. Therefore, a soporific speech is one that is boring and likely to make the audience sleepy.

entries.question_text: Select the world with right spelling-
entries.options_raw: (a) Schizophrenia (b) Seizophrania (c) Scizophrenia (d) Schizophrania
entries.explanation: Explanation: The correct spelling for the mental disorder is 'Schizophrenia'.

entries.question_text: Love for the whole world is called-
entries.options_raw: (a) philanthropy (b) misogyny (c) benevolence (d) misanthropy
entries.explanation: Explanation: Philanthropy is the desire to promote the welfare of others, expressed especially by the generous donation of money to good causes. It signifies a love for humanity. Misogyny is hatred of women, and misanthropy is hatred of mankind.

entries.question_text: When we want to mean a government by the richest class we use the term-
entries.options_raw: (a) Oligarchy (b) Plutocracy (c) Cryptocracy (d) Aristocracy
entries.explanation: Explanation: Plutocracy is a system of government where the wealthy class rules. Aristocracy is rule by the nobility, and Oligarchy is rule by a small group of people.

entries.question_text: Hospitals ____ the sick.
entries.options_raw: (a) operate (b) treat (c) admit (d) nurse
entries.explanation: Explanation: The primary function of a hospital is to provide medical care or 'treat' the sick. While they also admit, nurse, and operate, 'treat' is the most general and appropriate term for their overall function.

entries.question_text: The warning of the authority falls on deaf ears. Here ‘warning’ does the function of-
entries.options_raw: (a) adverb (b) adjective (c) verb (d) noun
entries.explanation: Explanation: In this sentence, 'warning' is preceded by the article 'The' and is the subject of the verb 'falls'. Words that function as subjects are nouns or pronouns. Therefore, 'warning' is a noun here.

entries.question_text: The word ‘culinary’ is related to-
entries.options_raw: (a) printing (b) cooking (c) dress (d) musical instruments
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Culinary' is an adjective that means related to cooking or the kitchen. For example, culinary skills are cooking skills.

entries.question_text: Identify the correct passive form of the sentence below : ‘Do you Know them’?

options.label: b
options.text: Would they be known by you?

entries.options_raw: (a) Are they known by you? (b) Would they be known by you? (c) Are they known with you? (d) Are they known to you?
entries.explanation: Explanation: The verb 'know' in the passive voice is followed by the preposition 'to', not 'by'. The active sentence is in the simple present tense, so the passive form will be: Am/Is/Are + subject + known to + object. Thus, 'Are they known to you?' is correct.

entries.question_text: ‘Panacea’ means-
entries.options_raw: (a) cure-all (b) pancreatic (c) widespread disease (d) gland
entries.explanation: Explanation: A panacea is a solution or remedy for all difficulties or diseases. Therefore, 'cure-all' is the correct meaning.

entries.question_text: what is the plural number of ‘ovum’?
entries.options_raw: (a) ovams (b) ovumes (c) onums (d) ova
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Ovum' is a Latin word for 'egg'. Its plural form follows Latin rules, making it 'ova'.

entries.question_text: কোন শব্দযুগলটি ভিন্ন?
entries.options_raw: (a) False , True (b) Sharp , Blunt (c) Love, Affection (d) Abundance , Scarcity
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Love' and 'Affection' are synonyms (words with similar meanings). The other pairs (False-True, Sharp-Blunt, Abundance-Scarcity) are antonyms (words with opposite meanings).

entries.question_text: ‘A christmas carol’ is a ____ by charles Dickens .
entries.options_raw: (a) ballad (b) sketch story (c) historical novel (d) short novel
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'A Christmas Carol' by Charles Dickens is a famous work of fiction that is too long to be a short story and too short to be a full-length novel. It is best described as a short novel or a novella.

entries.question_text: ‘There was a small reception following the wedding: The word ‘following’ in the sentence above is a/an _____.
entries.options_raw: (a) preposition (b) adjective (c) adverb (d) noun
entries.explanation: Explanation: In this sentence, 'following' means 'after' and shows the relationship between 'reception' and 'wedding'. It functions as a preposition.

entries.question_text: which of the following words has been formed with a prefix?
entries.options_raw: (a) amoral (b) authentic (c) amnesia (d) aspersions
entries.explanation: Explanation: The word 'amoral' is formed by adding the prefix 'a-' (meaning 'not' or 'without') to the root word 'moral'.

entries.question_text: লেফটেন্যান্ট জেনারেল শব্দের সঠিক ইংরেজি বানান কোনটি?
entries.options_raw: (ক) Lieaftenant (খ) Leaftenant (গ) Leiftenant (ঘ) Lieutenant
entries.explanation: সামরিক পদবি 'লেফটেন্যান্ট' এর সঠিক ইংরেজি বানান হলো 'Lieutenant'।

entries.question_text: ‘To be, or not to be, that is the question’ is a famous soliloquy from-
entries.options_raw: (a) Macbeth (b) King lear (c) Othello (d) Hamlet
entries.explanation: Explanation: This is the opening line of a famous soliloquy spoken by the titular character in William Shakespeare's play 'Hamlet'.

entries.question_text: ‘Geriatrics’ is the branch of medicine concerned with the diseases and care of-
entries.options_raw: (a) newly-weds (b) old women (c) newborn babies (d) old people
entries.explanation: Explanation: Geriatrics is the specialty of medicine that focuses on the health care of elderly people. It aims to promote health by preventing and treating diseases in older adults.

entries.question_text: নিচের উপমাটি পূর্ণকারী শব্দ কোনটি? Finger : Hand :: Leaf :
entries.options_raw: (ক) Flower (খ) Twig (গ) Tree (ঘ) Branch
entries.explanation: Explanation: The analogy is 'part to whole'. A finger is a part of a hand. Similarly, a leaf is a part of a twig (a small, thin branch of a tree or bush). Twig is the most immediate part a leaf is attached to.

entries.question_text: ‘Attested’ -এর বাংলা পরিভাষা কোনটি?
entries.options_raw: (ক) সত্যায়িত (খ) প্রত্যয়িত (গ) সত্যায়ন (ঘ) সংলগ্ন/সংলাগ
entries.explanation: 'Attested' শব্দের সঠিক ও প্রচলিত বাংলা পরিভাষা হলো 'সত্যায়িত'। এর অর্থ হলো কোনো দলিলের অনুলিপিকে মূল কপির সাথে মিলিয়ে সত্য বলে প্রত্যয়ন করা।

entries.question_text: A man whose wife has died is called a –
entries.options_raw: (a) widow (b) widower (c) spinster (d) bachelor
entries.explanation: Explanation: A man whose wife has died is called a 'widower'. A woman whose husband has died is a 'widow'.

entries.question_text: Which word is similar to ‘appal’?
entries.options_raw: (a) deceive (b) confuse (c) dismay (d) solicit
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Appal' means to greatly horrify, shock, or dismay someone. 'Dismay' (to cause someone to feel consternation and distress) is the closest synonym.

entries.question_text: Which word means the opposite of ‘dearth ‘ ?
entries.options_raw: (a) lack (b) abundance (c) poverty (d) shortage
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Dearth' means a scarcity or lack of something. Its opposite is 'abundance', which means a very large quantity of something.

entries.question_text: Tennyson’s ‘In Memoriam’ is an elegy on the death of –
entries.options_raw: (a) John Milton (b) John Keats (c) Arthur Henry Hallam (d) Sydney Smith
entries.explanation: Explanation: "In Memoriam A.H.H." is a long poem by Alfred, Lord Tennyson, written as an elegy for his close Cambridge friend Arthur Henry Hallam, who died suddenly.

entries.question_text: Identify the word which is spelt incorrectly :
entries.options_raw: (a) consciencious (b) perseverance (c) convalescence (d) maintenance
entries.explanation: Explanation: The correct spelling is 'conscientious'. The other spellings are correct.

entries.question_text: ‘You look terrific in that dress! ‘ The word ‘terrific’ in the above sentence means –
entries.options_raw: (a) excellent (b) funny (c) very ugly (d) horrible
entries.explanation: Explanation: In informal usage, 'terrific' means extremely good or excellent. It is a positive term here, contrasting with its literal meaning of 'causing terror'.

entries.question_text: Someone who is capricious is –

options.label: d
options.text: known for sudden changes in attitude or behavior

entries.options_raw: (a) easily irritated (b) wise and willing to cooperate (c) exceedingly conceited and arrogant (d) known for sudden changes in attitude or behavior
entries.correct_answer: (d) known for sudden changes in attitude or behavior
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Capricious' means given to sudden and unaccountable changes of mood or behavior; fickle.

entries.question_text: Identify the word which remains the same in its plural form :
entries.options_raw: (a) aircraft (b) intention (c) mouse (d) thesis
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Aircraft' is a noun that has the same form for both singular and plural. Other examples include sheep, deer, and fish.

entries.question_text: Identify the determiner in the following sentence : ‘I have no news for you.”
entries.options_raw: (a) have (b) news (c) no (d) for
entries.explanation: Explanation: A determiner is a word placed before a noun to specify quantity. 'No' is a determiner indicating the absence of something.

entries.question_text: A lost opportunity never returns. Here ‘lost’ is a –
entries.options_raw: (a) gerund (b) verbal noun (c) gerundial infinitive (d) participle
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Lost' is the past participle of the verb 'lose'. Here, it is used as an adjective to modify the noun 'opportunity'. A participle used as an adjective is called a participial adjective.

entries.question_text: The saying ‘enough is enough’ is used when you want-

options.label: c
options.text: something to continue until it’s enough

entries.options_raw: (a) something to continue (b) something to stop (c) something to continue until it’s enough (d) to tell instructions are clear
entries.explanation: Explanation: This phrase is used to say that something that has been happening for a long time must stop.

entries.question_text: He ran with great speed. The underlined part of the sentence is a –
entries.options_raw: (a) noun phrase (b) adverb phrase (c) adjective phrase (d) participle phrase
entries.explanation: Explanation: The prepositional phrase "with great speed" modifies the verb "ran" by describing how he ran. A phrase that modifies a verb is an adverb phrase.

entries.question_text: ‘We must not be late, else we will miss the train’ This is a –
entries.options_raw: (a) compound sentence (b) complex sentence (c) simple sentence (d) interrogative sentence
entries.explanation: Explanation: The sentence consists of two independent clauses ("We must not be late" and "we will miss the train") joined by the coordinating conjunction 'else'.

entries.question_text: Change the voice : ‘Who is calling me?”

options.label: c
options.text: By whom am I being called?

entries.options_raw: (a) By whom am I called? (b) By whom I am called? (c) By whom am I being called? (d) Whom am I called by?
entries.correct_answer: (c) By whom am I being called?
entries.explanation: Explanation: The active sentence is in the present continuous tense. Its passive form is: By whom + am/is/are + subject + being + past participle? This makes option (c) correct.

entries.question_text: An extra message added at the end of a letter after it is signed is called _____ .
entries.options_raw: (a) corrigendum (b) postscript (c) NB (d) RSVP
entries.explanation: Explanation: A postscript (often abbreviated as P.S.) is an additional thought added to a letter after it has been finished and signed.

entries.question_text: Sweet Helen ‘make me immortal with a kiss’ The sentence has been taken from the play –
entries.options_raw: (a) Romeo and Juliet (b) Caesar and Cleopatra (c) Doctor Faustus (d) Antony and Cleopatra
entries.explanation: Explanation: This famous line is from Christopher Marlowe's tragedy "Doctor Faustus", spoken by Faustus to a vision of Helen of Troy.

entries.question_text: ‘What’s in a name? That which we call a rose By any other name would smell as sweet’ – who said this?
entries.options_raw: (a) Juliet (b) Romeo (c) Portia (d) Rosalind
entries.explanation: Explanation: These lines are spoken by Juliet in Act II, Scene 2 of William Shakespeare's "Romeo and Juliet".

entries.question_text: ‘Man’s love is of man’s life a thing apart, Tis woman’s whole existence.’ This is taken from the poem of –
entries.options_raw: (a) P.BShelley (b) Lord Byron (c) John Keats (d) Edmund Spenser
entries.explanation: Explanation: This quote is from Lord Byron's epic satirical poem "Don Juan".

entries.question_text: Who translated the ‘Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam’ into English?
entries.options_raw: (a) Thomas Carlyle (b) Edward Fitzgerald (c) D.GRossetti (d) William Thackeray
entries.explanation: Explanation: Edward Fitzgerald's English translation of the "Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam," first published in 1859, is the most famous and influential version in the English-speaking world.

entries.question_text: ‘Ulysses’ is a novel written by –
entries.options_raw: (a) Joseph Conrad (b) Thomas Hardy (c) Charles Dickens (d) James Joyce
entries.explanation: Explanation: "Ulysses" is a landmark modernist novel by the Irish writer James Joyce, first published in 1922.

entries.question_text: The short story ‘The Diamond Necklace’ was written by –
entries.options_raw: (a) Guy de Maupassant (b) O Henry (c) Somerset Maugham (d) George Orwell
entries.explanation: Explanation: "The Diamond Necklace" is a famous short story with a twist ending, written by the French author Guy de Maupassant in 1884.

entries.question_text: ‘All the perfumes of Arabia will not sweeten this little hand’ – Who said this?
entries.options_raw: (a) Macbeth (b) Lady Macbeth (c) Lady Macduff (d) Macduff
entries.explanation: Explanation: This line is spoken by a guilt-ridden Lady Macbeth in Act V, Scene 1 of Shakespeare's "Macbeth" as she sleepwalks.

entries.question_text: ‘Where are the songs of Spring? Aye, where are they? Think not of them, thou hast thy music too.’ -Who wrote this?
entries.options_raw: (a) William Wordsworth (b) Robert Browning (c) John Keats (d) Samuel Coleridge
entries.explanation: Explanation: These lines are from the third stanza of John Keats's famous ode, "To Autumn".

entries.question_text: Who is the central character of ‘Wuthering Heights’ by Emily Bronte?
entries.options_raw: (a) MrEarnshaw (b) Catherine (c) Heathcliff (d) Hindley Earnshaw
entries.explanation: Explanation: Heathcliff, the brooding and vengeful foundling, is the central character and anti-hero of Emily Brontë's novel "Wuthering Heights".

entries.question_text: ‘The old order changeth, yielding place to new’ This line is extracted from Tennyson’s poem –
entries.options_raw: (a) The Lotos- Eaters (b) Tighouns (c) Locksley Hall (d) Morte d’ Arthur
entries.explanation: Explanation: This line is spoken by the dying King Arthur in Alfred, Lord Tennyson's poem "Morte d'Arthur".

entries.question_text: Who has written the poem “The Good Morrow”?
entries.options_raw: (a) George Herbert (b) Andrew Marvell (c) John Donne (d) Henry Vaughan
entries.explanation: Explanation: "The Good-Morrow" is a famous metaphysical poem by John Donne, published in his 1633 collection "Songs and Sonnets".

entries.question_text: ‘Please write to me at the above address’ The word ‘above’ in this sentence is a/an –
entries.options_raw: (a) noun (b) adjective (c) pronoun (d) adverb
entries.explanation: Explanation: Here, 'above' modifies the noun 'address' (the above address), so it functions as an adjective.

entries.question_text: In which sentence is the word ‘past’ used as a preposition?

options.label: a
options.text: Writing letters is a thing of the past .

options.label: b
options.text: I look back on the past without regret .

options.label: c
options.text: I called out to him as he ran past .

options.label: d
options.text: Tania was a wonderful singer, but she’s past her prime.

entries.options_raw: (a) Writing letters is a thing of the past . (b) I look back on the past without regret . (c) I called out to him as he ran past . (d) Tania was a wonderful singer, but she’s past her prime.
entries.correct_answer: (d) Tania was a wonderful singer, but she’s past her prime.
entries.explanation: Explanation: A preposition is followed by a noun or noun phrase. In sentence (d), 'past' is followed by the noun phrase 'her prime'. In (a) and (b) it's a noun; in (c) it's an adverb.

entries.question_text: The word ‘sibling’ means-
entries.options_raw: (a) a brother (b) a sister (c) a brother or sister (d) an infant
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Sibling' is a gender-neutral term for a brother or a sister.

entries.question_text: Fill in the blank: As she was talking, he suddenly broke__, saying, ‘That’s a lie!’
entries.options_raw: (a) off (b) in (c) down (d) into
entries.explanation: Explanation: The phrasal verb 'to break in' means to interrupt a conversation.

entries.question_text: Fill in the blank : You may go for a walk if you feel _____ it .
entries.options_raw: (a) about (b) on (c) like (d) for
entries.explanation: Explanation: The expression 'to feel like' doing something means to have the desire or inclination to do it.

entries.question_text: ‘The Rape of the Lock’ by Alexander Pope is a/an –
entries.options_raw: (a) epic (b) ballad (c) mock-heroic poem (d) elegy
entries.explanation: Explanation: "The Rape of the Lock" is a famous example of a mock-heroic poem, which satirically treats a trivial subject in the grand style of a classical epic.

entries.question_text: Which of the following is not an American poet?
entries.options_raw: (a) Robert Frost (b) W.B Yeats (c) Emily Dickinson (d) Langston Hughes
entries.explanation: Explanation: W. B. Yeats was an Irish poet. Robert Frost, Emily Dickinson, and Langston Hughes were all prominent American poets.

entries.question_text: William Shakespeare was born in-
entries.explanation: Explanation: William Shakespeare was born in Stratford-upon-Avon, England, in April 1564.

entries.question_text: “To win a prize is my ambition”. The underlined part of the sentence is a/an-
entries.options_raw: (a) adjective phrase (b) noun phrase (c) adverb phrase (d) conjunctional phrase
entries.explanation: Explanation: The infinitive phrase "To win a prize" acts as the subject of the verb "is". A phrase that functions as a subject, object, or complement is a noun phrase.

entries.question_text: Choose the word opposite in meaning to “terse”-
entries.options_raw: (a) concise (b) detailed (c) expressive (d) descriptive
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Terse' means sparing in the use of words; abrupt. Its opposite would be something long and full of information, making 'detailed' the best choice. 'Concise' is a synonym.

entries.question_text: “Who’s that?” In this sentence “that” is a/an-
entries.options_raw: (a) pronoun (b) conjunction (c) adjective (d) adverb
entries.explanation: Explanation: Here, "that" is a demonstrative pronoun, standing in for "that person".

entries.question_text: What is the noun form of the word “know”?
entries.options_raw: (a) knowing (b) knowledge (c) knowledgeable (d) Known
entries.explanation: Explanation: The noun form of the verb 'know' is 'knowledge', which means facts, information, and skills acquired through experience or education.

entries.question_text: “Why, then, ’tis none to you, for there is nothing either good or bad, but thinking makes it so”. This extract is taken from the drama-
entries.options_raw: (a) King Lear (b) Macbeth (c) As You Like It (d) Hamlet
entries.explanation: Explanation: This famous philosophical line is spoken by Prince Hamlet to Rosencrantz in Act II, Scene 2 of Shakespeare's "Hamlet".

entries.question_text: “Made weak by time and fate, but strong in will To strive to seek, to find, and not to yield” is taken from the poem written by-
entries.options_raw: (a) Robert Browning (b) Matthew Arnold (c) Alfred Tennyson (d) Lord Byron
entries.explanation: Explanation: These are the closing lines of the dramatic monologue "Ulysses" by the Victorian poet Alfred, Lord Tennyson.

entries.question_text: “Give somebody a piece of your mind” means to-

options.label: a
options.text: tell someone that you are very angry with them.

options.label: b
options.text: say exactly what you feel or think.

options.label: c
options.text: return or to help somebody return to a normal situation.

entries.options_raw: (a) tell someone that you are very angry with them. (b) say exactly what you feel or think. (c) return or to help somebody return to a normal situation. (d) give somebody mental peace
entries.correct_answer: (a) tell someone that you are very angry with them.
entries.explanation: Explanation: This idiom means to speak angrily to someone because they have done something wrong.

entries.question_text: “I shall help you provided you obey me”. Here the underlined word is a/an-
entries.options_raw: (a) adverb (b) adjective (c) conjunction (d) verb
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Provided' or 'provided that' is used as a subordinating conjunction to mean 'if' or 'on the condition that'.

entries.question_text: Identify the correct spelling
entries.options_raw: (a) questionaire (b) questionoir (c) questionnaire (d) questionair
entries.explanation: Explanation: The correct spelling for the set of printed or written questions with a choice of answers is 'questionnaire'.

entries.question_text: Which “but” is a preposition?

options.label: a
options.text: It is but right to admit our faults.

options.label: b
options.text: What can we do but sit and wait?

options.label: c
options.text: We tried hard, but did not succeed.

options.label: d
options.text: There is no one but likes him.

entries.options_raw: (a) It is but right to admit our faults. (b) What can we do but sit and wait? (c) We tried hard, but did not succeed. (d) There is no one but likes him.
entries.correct_answer: (b) What can we do but sit and wait?
entries.explanation: Explanation: In sentence (b), 'but' is used as a preposition meaning 'except' or 'other than'. In the other sentences, it is an adverb or a conjunction.

entries.question_text: Who is not a romantic poet?
entries.options_raw: (a) P. B. Shelley (b) S. T. Coleridge (c) John Keats (d) T. S. Eliot
entries.explanation: Explanation: T. S. Eliot was a leading figure of the Modernist movement in poetry. Shelley, Coleridge, and Keats were major poets of the Romantic era.

entries.question_text: In Shakespeare’s play Hamlet, Hamlet was prince of
entries.options_raw: (a) Norway (b) Britain (c) Denmark (d) France
entries.explanation: Explanation: The full title of the play is "The Tragedy of Hamlet, Prince of Denmark". The setting is the royal castle of Elsinore in Denmark.

entries.question_text: Adela Quested and Mrs. Moore are characters from the novel-
entries.options_raw: (a) David Copperfield (b) The Return of the Native (c) A Passage to India (d) Adam Bede
entries.explanation: Explanation: Adela Quested and Mrs. Moore are central characters in E. M. Forster's novel "A Passage to India" (1924).

entries.question_text: “Shylock” is a character in the play-
entries.options_raw: (a) Twelfth Night (b) The Merchant of Venice (c) Romeo and Juliet (d) Measure for Measure
entries.explanation: Explanation: Shylock is the principal antagonist, a Venetian Jewish moneylender, in William Shakespeare's play "The Merchant of Venice".

entries.question_text: ‘Vanity Fair’ is a novel written by-
entries.options_raw: (a) D. H. Lawrence (b) William Makepeace Thackeray (c) Joseph Conrad (d) Virgina Woolf
entries.explanation: Explanation: "Vanity Fair" is a satirical novel by William Makepeace Thackeray, first published in 1847–48, which critiques early 19th-century British society.

entries.question_text: ‘Pip’ is the protagonist in Charles Dickens’ novel-
entries.options_raw: (a) A Christmas Carol (b) A Tale of Two Cities (c) Oliver Twist (d) Great Expectations
entries.explanation: Explanation: Philip Pirrip, nicknamed Pip, is the protagonist and narrator in Charles Dickens's novel "Great Expectations" (1861).

entries.question_text: ‘Lady Chatterley’s Lover’ was written by the author of-
entries.options_raw: (a) Lord Jim (b) The Rainbow (c) Ulysses (d) A Passage to India
entries.explanation: Explanation: "Lady Chatterley's Lover" and "The Rainbow" were both written by the English author D. H. Lawrence.

entries.question_text: Identify the word that can be used as both singular and plural:
entries.options_raw: (a) wood (b) issue (c) fish (d) light
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Fish' can be both singular and plural (referring to multiple fish of the same species). 'Fishes' is used to refer to multiple species of fish.

entries.question_text: Find out the correct passive form of the sentence ‘Who taught you French?’

options.label: a
options.text: By whom you were taught French?

options.label: b
options.text: By whom French was taught you?

options.label: c
options.text: French was taught you by whom?

options.label: d
options.text: By whom were you taught French?

entries.options_raw: (a) By whom you were taught French? (b) By whom French was taught you? (c) French was taught you by whom? (d) By whom were you taught French?
entries.correct_answer: (d) By whom were you taught French?
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Who' becomes 'By whom'. The indirect object 'you' becomes the subject of the passive sentence. The correct interrogative structure is 'By whom + auxiliary verb + subject + ...?'.

entries.question_text: “The old man was tired of walking”. Here ‘walking’ is a/an-
entries.options_raw: (a) present participle (b) adjective (c) common noun (d) gerund
entries.explanation: Explanation: Here 'walking' is the object of the preposition 'of'. A verb ending in -ing that functions as a noun is a gerund.

entries.question_text: Which one is the correct sentence?
entries.options_raw: (a) The doctor found my pulse. (b) The doctor took my pulse. (c) The doctor examined my pulse. (d) The doctor saw my pulse.
entries.explanation: Explanation: The correct idiomatic expression for checking a pulse is "to take someone's pulse" or "to feel someone's pulse".

entries.question_text: ‘I will not let you go’. In this sentence ‘go’ is a/an-
entries.options_raw: (a) infinitive (b) gerund (c) participle (d) verbal noun
entries.explanation: Explanation: The verb 'let' is followed by a bare infinitive (an infinitive without 'to'). Here, 'go' is a bare infinitive.

entries.question_text: When Ushashi entered _____ the room everybody stopped talking.
entries.options_raw: (a) into (b) in (c) to (d) no preposition required
entries.explanation: Explanation: The verb 'enter' is a transitive verb when it means to go into a place, so it does not require a preposition. We say "enter the room," not "enter into the room."

entries.question_text: The play ‘The Birthday Party’ is written by-
entries.options_raw: (a) Samel Beckett (b) Henry Livings (c) Harold Pinter (d) Arthur Miller
entries.explanation: Explanation: "The Birthday Party" (1957) is the second full-length play by Nobel laureate Harold Pinter and is a classic example of the "Comedy of Menace".

entries.question_text: “Time held me green and dying Though I sang in my chains like the sea”. These lines have been quoted from Dylan Thomas’ poem-
entries.options_raw: (a) The Flower (b) Fern Hill (c) By Fire (d) After the Funeral
entries.explanation: Explanation: These are the final lines of the poem "Fern Hill" by the Welsh poet Dylan Thomas, reflecting on youth and the passage of time.

entries.question_text: One whose attitude is ‘eat, drink and be merry’ is-
entries.options_raw: (a) materialistic (b) epicurean (c) cynic (d) stoic
entries.explanation: Explanation: An 'epicurean' is a person devoted to sensual enjoyment, especially that derived from fine food and drink. This philosophy encourages enjoying life.

entries.question_text: ‘Was this the face that launch’d a thousand ships, And burnt the topless towers of Ilium? Who speaks the famous lines?
entries.options_raw: (a) Caesar (b) Antony (c) Faustus (d) Romeo
entries.explanation: Explanation: These lines are from Christopher Marlowe's play "Doctor Faustus," spoken by Faustus when he sees a vision of Helen of Troy.

entries.question_text: The Character ‘Alfred Doolittle’ is taken from Shaw’s play titled-
entries.options_raw: (a) Pygmalion (b) Man and Superman (c) The Doctor’s Dilemma (d) Mrs. Warren’s Profession
entries.explanation: Explanation: Alfred Doolittle is the father of the protagonist Eliza Doolittle in George Bernard Shaw's play "Pygmalion".

entries.question_text: The poem ‘The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock’ is written by-
entries.options_raw: (a) W. B. Yeats (b) T. S. Eliot (c) Walter Scott (d) Robert Browning
entries.explanation: Explanation: "The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock" is a seminal work of Modernist poetry, written by T. S. Eliot and published in 1915.

entries.question_text: Who is the author of the first scientific romance ‘The Time Machine’?
entries.options_raw: (a) H. G. Wells (b) Samuel Butler (c) Henry James (d) George Moore
entries.explanation: Explanation: H. G. Wells is often called the "father of science fiction," and his 1895 novel "The Time Machine" is considered a classic of the genre.

entries.question_text: ‘Call me if you have any problems regarding your work’. Here ‘regarding’ is a/an-
entries.options_raw: (a) gerund (b) apposition (c) preposition (d) conjunction
entries.explanation: Explanation: In this context, 'regarding' functions as a preposition, meaning 'about' or 'concerning'.

entries.question_text: Select the correct comparative form of the sentence. ‘A string of pearls was not so bright as her teeth.’

options.label: a
options.text: Her teeth was more brighter than a string of pearls.

options.label: b
options.text: Her teeth were brighter than a string of pearls.

options.label: c
options.text: A string of pearls was brighter than her teeth.

options.label: d
options.text: A string of pearls were very bright than her teeth.

entries.options_raw: (a) Her teeth was more brighter than a string of pearls. (b) Her teeth were brighter than a string of pearls. (c) A string of pearls was brighter than her teeth. (d) A string of pearls were very bright than her teeth.
entries.correct_answer: (b) Her teeth were brighter than a string of pearls.
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Teeth' is a plural noun, so it takes the plural verb 'were'. The comparative of 'bright' is 'brighter' (not 'more brighter'). The meaning is correctly reversed in the comparative form.

entries.question_text: ‘Come on, it’s time to go home’. Here ‘home’ is a/an-
entries.options_raw: (a) noun (b) verb (c) adjective (d) adverb
entries.explanation: Explanation: In the phrase "go home," 'home' functions as an adverb of place, indicating the direction or destination of the action 'go'.

entries.question_text: ‘Huffing and puffing, we arrived at the classroom door with only seven seconds to spare’. In this sentence the verb ‘arrived’ is-
entries.options_raw: (a) intransitive (b) transitive (c) causative (d) Defective
entries.explanation: Explanation: The verb 'arrived' does not take a direct object. It is followed by a prepositional phrase ('at the classroom door'). A verb that does not require a direct object is an intransitive verb.

entries.question_text: Which one of the following is a common gender?
entries.options_raw: (a) king (b) sovereign (c) emperor (d) Queen
entries.explanation: Explanation: A 'sovereign' is a supreme ruler, and can be either male (like a king or emperor) or female (like a queen). Therefore, it is a common gender noun.

entries.question_text: What is the correct indirect form of: He said, “You had better see a doctor”

options.label: ক
options.text: He advised him to see a doctor.

options.label: খ
options.text: He advised that he should see a doctor.

options.label: গ
options.text: He suggested that he seen a doctor.

options.label: ঘ
options.text: He proposed to see a doctor.

entries.options_raw: (ক) He advised him to see a doctor. (খ) He advised that he should see a doctor. (গ) He suggested that he seen a doctor. (ঘ) He proposed to see a doctor.
entries.correct_answer: (ক) He advised him to see a doctor.
entries.explanation: Reported speech-এ 'had better' থাকলে তা দ্বারা advice (উপদেশ) বোঝায়। তাই indirect করার সময় reporting verb হিসেবে 'advised' ব্যবহৃত হয় এবং 'had better' উঠে গিয়ে infinitive (to + verb) বসে। গঠন: Subject + advised + object + to + verb1।

entries.question_text: Identify the word that remains the same in plural form.
entries.options_raw: (ক) deer (খ) horse (গ) elephant (ঘ) tiger
entries.explanation: কিছু Noun আছে যাদের Singular এবং Plural form একই থাকে। যেমন: deer, sheep, fish, aircraft, series, species ইত্যাদি। তাই deer-এর plural রূপ deer-ই হবে।

entries.question_text: Which word is correct?
entries.options_raw: (ক) Furnitures (খ) Informations (গ) Sceneries (ঘ) Proceeds
entries.explanation: Furniture, Information, Scenery হলো Uncountable Noun, তাই এদের plural form হয় না। কিন্তু Proceeds (আয় বা লব্ধ অর্থ) শব্দটি একটি plural noun এবং এটি সবসময় 's' সহ ব্যবহৃত হয়।

entries.question_text: To doctor an animal means-
entries.options_raw: (ক) To treat it (খ) To sterilize it (গ) To poison it (ঘ) To cure it
entries.explanation: 'To doctor' verb টির একটি বিশেষ অর্থ হলো কোনো পশুকে খাসি করা বা তার প্রজনন ক্ষমতা নষ্ট করা (to sterilize)। সাধারণ চিকিৎসা করা (to treat/cure) বোঝালেও, 'to doctor an animal' বিশেষভাবে এই অর্থ প্রকাশ করে।

entries.question_text: The word “flying” in the sentence “Look at the flying bird” is-
entries.options_raw: (ক) gerund (খ) participle (গ) verbal noun (ঘ) gerundial infinitive
entries.explanation: যখন verb + ing যুক্ত শব্দ কোনো noun-এর আগে বসে adjective-এর কাজ করে, তখন তাকে Participle বলে। এখানে ‘flying’ শব্দটি ‘bird’ noun-টির অবস্থা (উড়ন্ত) প্রকাশ করছে, তাই এটি একটি Present Participle।

entries.question_text: Identify the determiner in the sentence “Bring me that book”
entries.options_raw: (ক) bring (খ) me (গ) that (ঘ) book
entries.explanation: Determiner হলো এমন শব্দ যা কোনো noun-এর আগে বসে সেটিকে নির্দেশ করে বা তার পরিমাণ বোঝায়। এখানে 'that' শব্দটি 'book' noun-টিকে নির্দিষ্ট করে বোঝাচ্ছে। তাই 'that' একটি Demonstrative Determiner।

entries.question_text: “A Passage to India” is written by-
entries.options_raw: (ক) E M Forster (খ) Nirad C Chauhuri (গ) Rudyard Kipling (ঘ) Walt Whitman
entries.explanation: "A Passage to India" (1924) ব্রিটিশ ঔপন্যাসিক E. M. Forster রচিত একটি বিখ্যাত উপন্যাস। ব্রিটিশ শাসনামলে ভারত ভ্রমণের অভিজ্ঞতা এর মূল ভিত্তি।

entries.question_text: What is the meaning of “musk”?

options.label: গ
options.text: a substance used in making perfume

entries.options_raw: (ক) a form of drama (খ) face cover (গ) a substance used in making perfume (ঘ) a disguise
entries.correct_answer: (গ) a substance used in making perfume
entries.explanation: Musk (মৃগনাভি বা কস্তুরী) হলো এক প্রকার সুগন্ধি দ্রব্য যা পুরুষ হরিণের নাভি থেকে পাওয়া যায় এবং সুগন্ধি তৈরিতে ব্যবহৃত হয়।

entries.question_text: Go and catch the falling star. Here the “falling” is-
entries.options_raw: (ক) An adverb (খ) A preposition (গ) An adjective (ঘ) A verb
entries.explanation: এখানে 'falling' (পড়ন্ত) শব্দটি 'star' noun-টিকে modify করছে, অর্থাৎ তারাটির অবস্থা বোঝাচ্ছে। Verb-এর সাথে ing যুক্ত হয়ে Adjective-এর কাজ করলে তাকে Participle Adjective বলে।

entries.question_text: Hasan has read most of the ____ of Shakespeare.
entries.options_raw: (ক) poem (খ) play (গ) drama (ঘ) works
entries.explanation: কোনো লেখকের সমগ্র সাহিত্যকর্মকে বোঝাতে 'works' (Plural) শব্দটি ব্যবহৃত হয়। Shakespeare-এর নাটক, কবিতা ইত্যাদির সমষ্টিকে 'works of Shakespeare' বলা হয়।

entries.question_text: Who wrote Dr. Zivago?
entries.options_raw: (ক) Maxim Gorky (খ) Boris Pastornak (গ) Fyodor Dostoevsky (ঘ) Leo Tolstoy
entries.explanation: "Doctor Zhivago" (ডক্টর জিভাগো) বিখ্যাত রুশ লেখক বরিস পাস্তেরনাক (Boris Pasternak) রচিত একটি উপন্যাস। এই উপন্যাসের জন্য তিনি ১৯৫৮ সালে নোবেল পুরস্কারে ভূষিত হন।

entries.question_text: Fill in the gap with the correct form of the verb: The police _____ informed yesterday.
entries.options_raw: (ক) is (খ) are (গ) was (ঘ) were
entries.explanation: 'Police' শব্দটি দেখতে singular হলেও এটি একটি collective noun যা সবসময় plural verb গ্রহণ করে। বাক্যে 'yesterday' থাকায় past tense হবে। সুতরাং সঠিক উত্তর 'were' (past plural)।

entries.question_text: Complete the sentence. If I were you, I ____ take the money.
entries.options_raw: (ক) shall (খ) will (গ) would (ঘ) may
entries.explanation: এটি একটি Second Conditional Sentence। এর গঠন হলো: If + Past Simple, ... would + Verb (base form)। এখানে 'If I were you' থাকায় পরের অংশে 'would take' বসবে।

entries.question_text: Would you please find out Bangladesh _____ the map?
entries.options_raw: (ক) in (খ) on (গ) over (ঘ) at
entries.explanation: মানচিত্রের (map) মতো কোনো পৃষ্ঠতলের উপর কোনো কিছু খুঁজে বের করা বা অবস্থান বোঝাতে preposition 'on' ব্যবহৃত হয়।

entries.question_text: Liza had given me two____
entries.options_raw: (ক) pair of jean (খ) pairs of jean (গ) pair of jeans (ঘ) pairs of jeans
entries.explanation: 'Jeans', 'trousers', 'scissors' ইত্যাদি noun গুলো plurale tantum অর্থাৎ এগুলো সবসময় plural form-এ থাকে। এদের সংখ্যা বোঝাতে 'pair of' ব্যবহৃত হয়। যেহেতু এখানে 'two' আছে, তাই 'pair'-এর plural 'pairs' হবে। সুতরাং সঠিক রূপ: two pairs of jeans।

entries.question_text: “Giving someone the cold shoulder” means-
entries.options_raw: (ক) To torture somebody (খ) To harm somebody (গ) To appreciate somebody (ঘ) To ignore somebody
entries.explanation: 'To give someone the cold shoulder' একটি idiom, যার অর্থ হলো কাউকে ইচ্ছাকৃতভাবে উপেক্ষা করা বা এড়িয়ে চলা।

entries.question_text: “September on the Jessore Road” is written by-
entries.options_raw: (ক) Madhusudan Dutt (খ) Allen Ginsberg (গ) Kaisar Hoq (ঘ) Vikram Seth
entries.explanation: "September on Jessore Road" বাংলাদেশের মুক্তিযুদ্ধকালে শরণার্থীদের দুর্দশা নিয়ে লেখা একটি বিখ্যাত কবিতা। এর রচয়িতা মার্কিন কবি অ্যালেন গিন্সবার্গ (Allen Ginsberg)।

entries.question_text: Identify the correctly spelled one.
entries.options_raw: (ক) Caesarian (খ) Ceasarian (গ) Ciserian (ঘ) Scissorian
entries.explanation: Caesarian (সিজারিয়ান) অর্থ অস্ত্রোপচারের মাধ্যমে সন্তান প্রসব। সঠিক বানানটি হলো C-A-E-S-A-R-I-A-N।

entries.question_text: What is the function of a topic sentence?
entries.options_raw: (ক) To introduce the topic (খ) To analyse the topic (গ) To present the main idea (ঘ) To expand the idea
entries.explanation: একটি Topic Sentence সাধারণত অনুচ্ছেদের শুরুতে বসে এবং ওই অনুচ্ছেদের মূল ধারণা বা বক্তব্য (main idea) উপস্থাপন করে। পরবর্তী বাক্যগুলো এই main idea-কে ব্যাখ্যা বা সমর্থন করে।

entries.question_text: For God’s sake, hold your tongue and let me love” occurs in a novel by-
entries.options_raw: (ক) Jane Austin (খ) Syed Waliullah (গ) Somerset Maugham (ঘ) Rabindranath Tagore
entries.explanation: এই বিখ্যাত লাইনটি ইংরেজ কবি John Donne-এর "The Canonization" কবিতার। রবীন্দ্রনাথ ঠাকুর তাঁর 'শেষের কবিতা' উপন্যাসে চরিত্র অমিত রায়ের মাধ্যমে এই লাইনটি উদ্ধৃত করেছেন। তাই প্রদত্ত বিকল্পগুলোর মধ্যে রবীন্দ্রনাথ ঠাকুর সঠিক উত্তর।

entries.question_text: What is the antonym for the word ‘deformation’?
entries.options_raw: (a) distortion (b) contortion (c) wholeness (d) disfigurement
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Deformation' means the action of distorting or disfiguring the shape or structure of something. Its opposite is 'wholeness', meaning the state of being complete or unbroken.

entries.question_text: Words inscribed on a tomb is an-
entries.options_raw: (a) epitome (b) epithet (c) episode (d) epitaph
entries.explanation: Explanation: An 'epitaph' is a phrase or form of words written in memory of a person who has died, especially as an inscription on a tombstone.

entries.question_text: The phrase ‘dog days’ means-
entries.options_raw: (a) hot weather (b) cold shower (c) rain-soaked streets (d) ice storm
entries.explanation: Explanation: The 'dog days' of summer are the hottest and most sultry part of the season.

entries.question_text: Which gender is the word ‘orphan’?
entries.options_raw: (a) neuter (b) feminine (c) common (d) masculine
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Orphan' is a common gender noun because it can refer to either a male or a female child whose parents are dead.

entries.question_text: Who wrote the play “The Way of the World”?
entries.options_raw: (a) William Shakespeare (b) William Congreve (c) Ben Jonson (d) Oscar Wilde
entries.explanation: Explanation: "The Way of the World" is a famous Restoration comedy play written by the English playwright William Congreve in 1700.

entries.question_text: “Better to reign in Hell, than serve in Heav’n.” –Who wrote this?
entries.options_raw: (a) Geoffrey Chaucer (b) Christopher Marlowe (c) John Milton (d) P. B. Shelley
entries.explanation: Explanation: This famous line is spoken by the character Satan in John Milton's epic poem "Paradise Lost" (Book I).

entries.question_text: Who is not an Irish writer?
entries.options_raw: (a) Oscar Wilde (b) James Joyce (c) Jonathan Swift (d) D. H. Lawrence
entries.explanation: Explanation: D. H. Lawrence was an English writer. Oscar Wilde, James Joyce, and Jonathan Swift were all prominent Irish writers.

entries.question_text: ‘A herd of cattle is passing.’ The underlined word is a/an –
entries.options_raw: (a) adverb (b) adjective (c) collective noun (d) abstract noun
entries.explanation: Explanation: A collective noun is a word that refers to a group of people or things. 'Herd' refers to a group of cattle.

entries.question_text: What is the adjective form of the word ‘people’?
entries.options_raw: (a) populous (b) popular (c) popularity (d) popularize
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Populous' is the adjective form, meaning 'having a large population'. 'Popular' means liked by many people.

entries.question_text: ‘He contemplated marrying his cousin.’ Here ‘marrying’ is a/an-
entries.options_raw: (a) present participle (b) gerund (c) verb (d) infinitive
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Marrying' is the object of the verb 'contemplated'. A verb form ending in '-ing' that functions as a noun is called a gerund.

entries.question_text: ‘No Second Troy’ is a-
entries.options_raw: (a) short story (b) novel (c) poem (d) drama
entries.explanation: Explanation: "No Second Troy" is a famous poem by the Irish poet W. B. Yeats, written about his muse, Maud Gonne.

entries.question_text: Who is not a modern poet?
entries.options_raw: (a) W. B. Yeats (b) W. H. Auden (c) John Keats (d) T. S. Eliot
entries.explanation: Explanation: John Keats was a leading figure of the second generation of Romantic poets (early 19th century). The others are major figures of the Modernist period (late 19th and early 20th centuries).

entries.question_text: Who is the author of the novel ‘The God of Small Things’?.
entries.options_raw: (a) Thomas Hardy (b) Jhumpa Lahiri (c) R. K. Narayan (d) Arundhati Roy
entries.explanation: Explanation: "The God of Small Things" is the debut novel of Indian writer Arundhati Roy, which won the Booker Prize in 1997.

entries.question_text: Which of the following novels is not written by an English writer?
entries.options_raw: (a) A Passage to India (b) Sons and Lovers (c) One Hundred Years of Solitude (d) Pride and Prejudice
entries.explanation: Explanation: "One Hundred Years of Solitude" was written by the Colombian novelist Gabriel García Márquez. The others were written by English authors E.M. Forster, D.H. Lawrence, and Jane Austen.

entries.question_text: A speech full of too many words is-
entries.options_raw: (a) a big speech (b) maiden speech (c) a verbose speech (d) an unimportant speech
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Verbose' means using or expressed in more words than are needed. Therefore, a speech with too many words is a verbose speech.

entries.question_text: Who is the poet of the poem “Ozymandias”?
entries.options_raw: (a) P. B. Shelley (b) William Wordsworth (c) S. T. Coleridge (d) John Keats
entries.explanation: Explanation: "Ozymandias" is a famous sonnet written by the English Romantic poet Percy Bysshe Shelley.

entries.question_text: ‘Moby Dick’, a novel, was written by –
entries.options_raw: (a) Herman Melville (b) Nathaniel Hawthorne (c) Mark Twain (d) William Faulkner
entries.explanation: Explanation: "Moby-Dick; or, The Whale" is an 1851 novel by American writer Herman Melville.

entries.question_text: ‘If Winter comes, can Spring be far behind?’ – Who wrote this?
entries.options_raw: (a) William Blake (b) S. T. Coleridge (c) Lord Byron (d) P. B. Shelley
entries.explanation: Explanation: This is the famous concluding line of Percy Bysshe Shelley's poem "Ode to the West Wind".

entries.question_text: O’ Henry was from –
entries.options_raw: (a) Canada (b) America (c) England (d) Ireland
entries.explanation: Explanation: O. Henry was the pen name of William Sydney Porter, a famous American short-story writer known for his surprise endings.

entries.question_text: Where is the setting of the play ‘Hamlet’?
entries.options_raw: (a) England (b) Italy (c) France (d) Denmark
entries.explanation: Explanation: The setting for William Shakespeare's tragedy "Hamlet" is the royal castle of Elsinore in Denmark.

entries.question_text: The word ‘to genuflect’ means –
entries.options_raw: (a) to be genuine (b) to reflect (c) to bend the knee (d) to be flexible
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'To genuflect' means to lower one's body briefly by bending one knee to the ground, typically in worship or as a sign of respect.

entries.question_text: Fill in the blank: She went to New Market _____.
entries.options_raw: (a) on foot (b) on feet (c) by foot (d) by walking
entries.explanation: Explanation: The correct and idiomatic phrase for walking somewhere is 'on foot'.

entries.question_text: Fill in the gap: Birds fly ___ in the sky.
entries.options_raw: (a) random (b) at large (c) at a stitch (d) are long
entries.explanation: Explanation: The phrase 'at large' means free or unconfined. The sentence means birds fly freely in the sky.

entries.question_text: Who is the author of ‘Jane Eyre’?
entries.options_raw: (a) Charlotte Brontë (b) Emily Brontë (c) Jane Austen (d) Mary Shelley
entries.explanation: Explanation: "Jane Eyre" is a famous novel by the English writer Charlotte Brontë, published in 1847.

entries.question_text: The most famous romantic poet of English literature is –
entries.options_raw: (a) John Dryden (b) Alexander Pope (c) William Wordsworth (d) T. S. Eliot
entries.explanation: Explanation: William Wordsworth is considered one of the leading figures and pioneers of the English Romantic Movement in literature.

entries.question_text: Identify the correct synonym for the word ‘magnanimous’.
entries.options_raw: (a) unkind (b) generous (c) revengeful (d) friendly
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Magnanimous' means generous or forgiving, especially toward a rival or less powerful person. 'Generous' is the closest synonym.

entries.question_text: Choose the right form of verb: It is high time we (act) on the matter.
entries.options_raw: (a) are acting (b) acted (c) have acted (d) could act
entries.explanation: Explanation: The phrase 'It is high time' is followed by a subject and a verb in the past simple tense to express that something should have already been done.

entries.question_text: What is the noun form of the word ‘laugh’?
entries.options_raw: (a) laughing (b) laughable (c) laughter (d) laughingly
entries.explanation: Explanation: The noun form of the verb 'laugh' is 'laughter', which means the action or sound of laughing.

entries.question_text: Identify the word which is spelt incorrectly:
entries.options_raw: (a) fluctuation (b) remission (c) ocassion (d) decision
entries.explanation: Explanation: The correct spelling is 'occasion' (with double 'c' and single 's').

entries.question_text: Change the voice: ‘Nobody trusts a traitor.’

options.label: b
options.text: A traitor should not be trusted.

options.label: d
options.text: A traitor is not trusted by anybody.

entries.options_raw: (a) A traitor is trusted.. (b) A traitor should not be trusted. (c) Everybody hates a traitor. (d) A traitor is not trusted by anybody.
entries.correct_answer: (d) A traitor is not trusted by anybody.
entries.explanation: Explanation: In passive voice, the object 'a traitor' becomes the subject. 'Nobody' is an indefinite pronoun, so it becomes 'not... by anybody' or simply 'not trusted' if the agent is omitted.

entries.question_text: ___ was both a poet and a painter.
entries.options_raw: (a) John Keats (b) Spenser (c) William Blake (d) John Donne
entries.explanation: Explanation: William Blake was a prominent figure in the Romantic Age, renowned for both his visionary poetry and his intricate paintings and engravings.

entries.question_text: Identify the correct sentence:
entries.options_raw: (a) The girl burst out tears. (b) The girl burst into tears. (c) The girl burst with tears. (d) The girl bursted out tears.
entries.explanation: Explanation: The correct idiom is 'to burst into tears', meaning to suddenly start crying. The verb 'burst' has the same form for past tense.

entries.question_text: The phrase ‘sine die’ means –
entries.options_raw: (a) half-heartedly (b) doubtfully (c) fixed (d) uncertain
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Sine die' is a Latin term meaning 'without a day appointed' or 'indefinitely'. It is used when a meeting is adjourned without a set date for the next meeting, thus the future is uncertain.

entries.question_text: What kind of play is ‘Julius Caesar’?
entries.options_raw: (a) romantic (b) anti-romantic (c) comedy (d) historical
entries.explanation: Explanation: William Shakespeare's "Julius Caesar" is classified as a historical play or a Roman tragedy, as it is based on events from Roman history.

entries.question_text: Do you have any money ___ you? Fill in the blank with appropriate preposition:
entries.options_raw: (a) to (b) over (c) in (d) on
entries.explanation: Explanation: The idiomatic expression 'to have money on you' means to have money with you, in your possession at that moment.

entries.question_text: Select the appropriate preposition: ‘Are you doing’ anything special ___ the weekend?’
entries.options_raw: (a) at (b) with (c) on (d) for
entries.explanation: Explanation: In British English, 'at the weekend' is standard. In American English, 'on the weekend' is more common. Both are considered correct, but 'at' is often preferred in formal contexts.

entries.question_text: What is the plural form of ‘sheep’?
entries.options_raw: (a) sheeps (b) sheep (c) sheepes (d) sheepses
entries.explanation: Explanation: Some nouns have the same form for both singular and plural. 'Sheep' is one of them (one sheep, many sheep). Other examples include deer, fish, etc.

entries.question_text: ‘Sweet are the uses of adversity’ is quoted from Shakespeare’s –
entries.options_raw: (a) Julius Caesar (b) Macbeth (c) Comedy of Errors (d) As you Like It
entries.explanation: Explanation: This famous line is spoken by Duke Senior in Act II, Scene I of William Shakespeare's comedy 'As You Like It'.

entries.question_text: What is the verb form of the word ‘ability’?
entries.options_raw: (a) capable (b) inability (c) enable (d) unable
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Enable' is the verb form, meaning 'to make someone able to do something'. 'Capable' is an adjective, and 'inability' is a noun.

entries.question_text: The word ‘equivocation’ refers to –

options.label: b
options.text: two contradictory things in the same statement

entries.options_raw: (a) stating like an author (b) two contradictory things in the same statement (c) free expression of opinions (d) a true statement
entries.correct_answer: (b) two contradictory things in the same statement
entries.explanation: Explanation: Equivocation is the use of ambiguous language to conceal the truth or to avoid committing oneself. It often involves saying something that can be interpreted in two different, often contradictory, ways.

entries.question_text: “Life’s but a walking shadow, a poor player, That struts and frets his hour upon the stage, And then is heard no more;” These memorable lines in Shakespearean tragedy are spoken by –
entries.options_raw: (a) Lady Macbeth (b) Banquo (c) Duncan (d) Macbeth
entries.explanation: Explanation: This is part of a famous soliloquy spoken by Macbeth in Act V, Scene V of Shakespeare's 'Macbeth', upon hearing of his wife's death.

entries.question_text: Which of the following words is spelt correctly?
entries.options_raw: (a) authoratative (b) autheritative (c) authoritative (d) authoratative
entries.explanation: Explanation: The correct spelling of the word meaning 'able to be trusted as being accurate or true' is 'authoritative'.

entries.question_text: Find out the active form of the sentence: “By whom can our country be saved?”

options.label: b
options.text: Our country has been saved by who?

entries.options_raw: (a) Who can save our country? (b) Our country has been saved by who? (c) Who save our country? (d) Who will save our country?
entries.explanation: Explanation: The passive modal 'can be saved' becomes the active modal 'can save'. The passive subject 'our country' becomes the active object, and 'By whom' becomes the active subject 'Who'.

entries.question_text: “All changed, changed utterly: A terrible beauty is born.” This extract is taken from W. B. Yeats’ poem titled—
entries.options_raw: (a) No Second Troy (b) Easter 1916 (c) The Second Coming (d) The Wild Swans at Coole
entries.explanation: Explanation: These are the closing lines of the first stanza of W. B. Yeats' poem "Easter, 1916," which reflects on the Easter Rising in Ireland.

entries.question_text: Identify the correct passive form: ‘Do not close the door.’

options.label: b
options.text: Let not the door be closed.

entries.options_raw: (a) Let not the door close. (b) Let not the door be closed. (c) Let not the door close. (d) Let not door closed.
entries.correct_answer: (b) Let not the door be closed.
entries.explanation: Explanation: The passive form of a negative imperative sentence starts with 'Let not', followed by the object, 'be', and the past participle of the verb.

entries.question_text: The poetic drama ‘Murder in the Cathedral’ was written by—
entries.options_raw: (a) Harlod Pinter (b) G. B. Shaw (c) T. S. Eliot (d) Samuel Beckett
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Murder in the Cathedral' is a verse drama by T. S. Eliot, first performed in 1935, that portrays the assassination of Archbishop Thomas Becket.

entries.question_text: ‘All for Love’ is a drama written by—
entries.options_raw: (a) John Dryden (b) William Congreve (c) John Bunyan (d) Francis Bacon
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'All for Love' is a heroic drama by John Dryden, written in 1677. It is a retelling of the story of Antony and Cleopatra.

entries.question_text: Sitting happily, the chicken laid eggs. The underlined part is a/an—
entries.options_raw: (a) noun clause (b) subordinate clause (c) independent clause (d) coordinate clause
entries.explanation: Explanation: "Sitting happily" is a participle phrase that modifies "the chicken". It functions as an adverbial phrase, which is a type of subordinate or dependent clause/phrase, as it cannot stand alone as a complete sentence.

entries.question_text: Caliban is an important character from Shakespeare’s—
entries.options_raw: (a) The Tempest (b) Hamlet (c) Macbeth (d) Othello
entries.explanation: Explanation: Caliban is a key character in William Shakespeare's play 'The Tempest'. He is the monstrous son of the witch Sycorax.

entries.question_text: What kind of noun is ‘river’?
entries.options_raw: (a) Material (b) Collective (c) Proper (d) Common
entries.explanation: Explanation: A common noun is a name for a general class of people, places, or things (e.g., river, city, boy). A proper noun names a specific one (e.g., Padma, Dhaka, Rahim).

entries.question_text: ‘Caesar and Cleopatra’ is—

options.label: d
options.text: a novel by S. T. Coleridge

entries.options_raw: (a) a tragedy by William Shakespeare (b) a poem by Lord Byron (c) a play by Bernard Shaw (d) a novel by S. T. Coleridge
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Caesar and Cleopatra' is a historical play written in 1898 by the Irish playwright George Bernard Shaw.

entries.question_text: Identify the right tense: ‘My father _____ before I came’.
entries.options_raw: (a) would be leaving (b) had been leaving (c) had left (d) will leave
entries.explanation: Explanation: When two actions happened in the past, the action that occurred earlier is expressed in the past perfect tense (had + past participle), and the later action is in the simple past tense.

entries.question_text: Which of the following words is spelt incorrectly?
entries.options_raw: (a) reminescence (b) glycerin (c) idiosyncrasy (d) lexicography
entries.explanation: Explanation: The correct spelling is 'reminiscence'.

entries.question_text: Who wrote the picaresque novel titled ‘Tom Jones’?
entries.options_raw: (a) Samuel Richardson (b) Horace Walpole (c) Henry Fielding (d) Laurence Sterne
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'The History of Tom Jones, a Foundling', often known simply as 'Tom Jones', is a comic novel by the English playwright and novelist Henry Fielding. It is a classic picaresque novel.

entries.question_text: The story of ‘Moby Dick’ centers on—
entries.options_raw: (a) a mermaid (b) a whale (c) a crocodile (d) a shark
entries.explanation: Explanation: Herman Melville's novel 'Moby-Dick' is about the obsessive quest of Captain Ahab to hunt a giant white sperm whale named Moby Dick.

entries.question_text: ‘He prayeth best, who loveth best.’ —Who said it?
entries.options_raw: (a) John Milton (b) John Donne (c) Lord Byron (d) S.T. Coleridge
entries.explanation: Explanation: This line is from Samuel Taylor Coleridge's famous poem, "The Rime of the Ancient Mariner".

entries.question_text: The controlling sentence of a paragraph is known as—
entries.options_raw: (a) content modulator (b) terminator (c) thesis statement (d) topic sentence
entries.explanation: Explanation: A topic sentence is the sentence in a paragraph that summarizes the main idea of that paragraph.

entries.question_text: Choose the correct comparative form of the sentence: ‘Very few boys are as industrious as Zaman.’

options.label: a
options.text: Zaman is one of the most industrious boys.

options.label: b
options.text: Zaman is more industrious than most other boys.

options.label: c
options.text: Zaman is really industrious like other boys.

options.label: d
options.text: Zaman is as industrious as other boys.

entries.options_raw: (a) Zaman is one of the most industrious boys. (b) Zaman is more industrious than most other boys. (c) Zaman is really industrious like other boys. (d) Zaman is as industrious as other boys.
entries.correct_answer: (b) Zaman is more industrious than most other boys.
entries.explanation: Explanation: The positive degree sentence structure 'Very few... as... as' is converted to the comparative form '... more... than most other...'.

entries.question_text: Identify the appropriate preposition: Your opinion is identical __ mine.
entries.options_raw: (a) for (b) in (c) with (d) by
entries.explanation: Explanation: The adjective 'identical' is followed by the preposition 'with' or 'to'. 'With' is the more common choice in this context.

entries.question_text: ‘Paradise Lost’ attempted to—

options.label: a
options.text: justify the ways of man to God

options.label: b
options.text: show that Satan and God have equal power

options.label: c
options.text: justify the ways of God to man

options.label: d
options.text: explain why both good and evil are necessary

entries.options_raw: (a) justify the ways of man to God (b) show that Satan and God have equal power (c) justify the ways of God to man (d) explain why both good and evil are necessary
entries.correct_answer: (c) justify the ways of God to man
entries.explanation: Explanation: In the opening of his epic poem 'Paradise Lost', John Milton explicitly states his purpose is to "justify the ways of God to men".

entries.question_text: “Oh, lift me as a wave, a leaf, a cloud! I fall upon the thorns of life! I bleed!” The extract is taken from P. B. Shelley’s poem—
entries.options_raw: (a) The Cloud (b) To a Skylark (c) Ode to the West Wind (d) Adonais
entries.explanation: Explanation: These powerful lines are from Percy Bysshe Shelley's famous "Ode to the West Wind," where the poet asks the wind to lift his spirit.

entries.question_text: Who wrote the short story ‘The Ant and the Grasshopper’?
entries.options_raw: (a) Guy de Maupassant (b) W. Somerset Maugham (c) J. K. Rawlings (d) O’ Henry
entries.explanation: Explanation: "The Ant and the Grasshopper" is a short story by the British writer W. Somerset Maugham, which provides a modern twist on the classic Aesop's fable.

entries.question_text: The word ‘vital’ is a/an—
entries.options_raw: (a) noun (b) adverb (c) adjective (d) verb
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Vital' means absolutely necessary or important; essential. It is used to describe a noun (e.g., a vital role), so it is an adjective.

entries.question_text: ‘To get along with’ means—
entries.options_raw: (a) to adjust (b) to interest (c) to accompany (d) to walk
entries.explanation: Explanation: The phrasal verb 'to get along with' means to have a harmonious or friendly relationship, which requires adjusting to one another.

entries.question_text: The synonym for ‘panoramic’ is—
entries.options_raw: (a) scenic (b) narrow (c) limited (d) restricted
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Panoramic' means a view of a wide area. 'Scenic' also refers to providing or relating to views of natural scenery, making it the best synonym.

entries.question_text: The antonym for ‘slothful’ is—
entries.options_raw: (a) playful (b) sluggish (c) energetic (d) quarrelsome
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Slothful' means lazy or indolent. Its direct opposite is 'energetic', which means active and full of vitality.

entries.question_text: Alexander Pope’s ‘Essay on Man’ is a—
entries.options_raw: (a) novel (b) treatise (c) short story (d) poem
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'An Essay on Man' is a philosophical poem written by Alexander Pope in heroic couplets. It explores the nature of humanity and its place in the universe.

entries.question_text: ‘By and large’ means—
entries.options_raw: (a) everywhere (b) very large (c) mostly (d) far away
entries.explanation: Explanation: The idiom 'by and large' means on the whole, in general, or mostly.

entries.question_text: Francis Bacon is an illustrious—
entries.options_raw: (a) essayist (b) dramatist (c) novelist (d) journalist
entries.explanation: Explanation: Francis Bacon, a key figure in the Scientific Revolution, is renowned as the "father of the English essay" for his concise and aphoristic prose style.

entries.question_text: ‘He could not win but learnt a lot.’ Which part of speech is the word ‘but’?
entries.options_raw: (a) an adverb (b) a verb (c) an adjective (d) a conjunction
entries.explanation: Explanation: Here, 'but' is a coordinating conjunction, connecting two independent clauses ('He could not win' and 'he learnt a lot').

entries.question_text: She insisted on _____ leaving the house.
entries.options_raw: (a) he (b) him (c) himself (d) his
entries.explanation: Explanation: A gerund ('leaving') is preceded by a possessive pronoun or noun (here, 'his') to indicate who is performing the action. This is known as a possessive with gerund construction.

entries.question_text: The phrase ‘Achilles heel’ means–
entries.options_raw: (a) a strong point (b) a strong solution (c) a weak point (d) a permanent solution
entries.explanation: Explanation: An 'Achilles' heel' is a fatal weakness in spite of overall strength, originating from the Greek myth of Achilles.

entries.question_text: He does not adhere __ any principle.
entries.options_raw: (a) by (b) in (c) at (d) to
entries.explanation: Explanation: The verb 'adhere' is followed by the preposition 'to', meaning to stick to or follow a rule, belief, or principle.

entries.question_text: Millennium is a period of –
entries.options_raw: (a) 100 year (b) 1000 year (c) 1 million year (d) 1 billion year
entries.explanation: Explanation: A millennium is a period of one thousand years. A century is 100 years.

entries.question_text: Identify the passive form of the following sentence: “Who has broken this Jug?”

options.label: a
options.text: By whom has this Jug been broken?

options.label: b
options.text: By whom has this Jug broken?

options.label: c
options.text: By whom this Jug has been broken?

options.label: d
options.text: Whom has this Jug been broken?

entries.options_raw: (a) By whom has this Jug been broken? (b) By whom has this Jug broken? (c) By whom this Jug has been broken? (d) Whom has this Jug been broken?
entries.correct_answer: (a) By whom has this Jug been broken?
entries.explanation: Explanation: In a passive interrogative sentence, 'Who' becomes 'By whom'. The structure is: By whom + auxiliary verb + subject + been + past participle? This makes option (a) the correct form.

entries.question_text: Who is not a Victorian Poet?
entries.options_raw: (a) Alfred Tennyson (b) Robert Browning (c) William Wordsworth (d) Matthew Arnold
entries.explanation: Explanation: William Wordsworth was a major poet of the Romantic Period (late 18th to early 19th century). Tennyson, Browning, and Arnold are prominent poets of the Victorian Period (1837-1901).

entries.question_text: Which of the following novels was written by George Orwell?
entries.options_raw: (a) 1984 (b) Brave New World (c) A Clockwork Orange (d) For Whom the Bell Tolls
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Nineteen Eighty-Four' (1984) is a famous dystopian novel by English writer George Orwell. 'Brave New World' was written by Aldous Huxley.

entries.question_text: Identify the correct sentence:

options.label: b
options.text: She speaks the English like English

options.label: c
options.text: She speaks the English like the English

options.label: d
options.text: She speaks English like the English

entries.options_raw: (a) She speaks English like English (b) She speaks the English like English (c) She speaks the English like the English (d) She speaks English like the English
entries.correct_answer: (d) She speaks English like the English
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'English' refers to the language (no article). 'The English' refers to the people of England. So, the sentence means she speaks the language as the people of England do.

entries.question_text: When one makes a promise, one must not go________ on it.
entries.options_raw: (a) forward (b) back (c) by (d) around
entries.explanation: Explanation: The phrasal verb 'to go back on' means to fail to keep a promise.

entries.question_text: I can’t put up with him anymore. Here, “put up with” means:
entries.options_raw: (a) To protect (b) To terminate (c) To tolerate (d) To prevent
entries.explanation: Explanation: The phrasal verb 'to put up with' means to endure or tolerate someone or something unpleasant.

entries.question_text: The poem ”To his Coy Mistress” was written by-
entries.options_raw: (a) Andrew Marvell (b) John Donne (c) George Herbert (d) Henry Vaughan
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'To His Coy Mistress' is a famous metaphysical poem written by Andrew Marvell, a 17th-century English poet.

entries.question_text: The synonym of ‘altitude’ is –
entries.options_raw: (a) height (b) width (c) length (d) depth
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Altitude' refers to the height of an object or point in relation to sea level or ground level.

entries.question_text: The character, Elizabeth Bennet, appears in the novel-
entries.options_raw: (a) Pride and Prejudice (b) Tess of the D’Urbervilles (c) Wuthering Heights (d) Jane Eyre
entries.explanation: Explanation: Elizabeth Bennet is the protagonist of Jane Austen's famous 1813 novel 'Pride and Prejudice'.

entries.question_text: This could have worked if I _______ been more far-sighted.
entries.options_raw: (a) have (b) had (c) might (d) would
entries.explanation: Explanation: This is a third conditional sentence expressing an unreal past condition. The structure for the 'if' clause is 'if + subject + past perfect (had + past participle)'.

entries.question_text: What may be considered courteous in one culture may be arrogant in another. Here the underlined word, ”arrogant” means—
entries.options_raw: (a) rude (b) gracious (c) coarse (d) pretentious
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Arrogant' means having or revealing an exaggerated sense of one's own importance or abilities. In this context, it contrasts with 'courteous' (polite) and is best matched by 'rude' (impolite).

entries.question_text: Don Juan was composed by—
entries.options_raw: (a) W.B. Yeats (b) E.B. Browning (c) George Gordon Byron (d) Alexander Pope
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Don Juan' is a satirical epic poem by the Romantic poet Lord Byron (George Gordon Byron).

entries.question_text: Identify the imperative sentence:
entries.options_raw: (a) Shut up! (b) Shahin is playing football. (c) I shall cook dinner now. (d) What is your name?
entries.explanation: Explanation: An imperative sentence gives a command, order, or request. 'Shut up!' is a direct command.

entries.question_text: ”Black Death” is the name of a—
entries.options_raw: (a) fever (b) black fever (c) plague pandemic (d) death of black people
entries.explanation: Explanation: The Black Death was a devastating bubonic plague pandemic that struck Europe and Asia in the mid-14th century.

entries.question_text: ‘Ulysses’ is a poem written by—
entries.options_raw: (a) Robert Browning (b) Wordsworth (c) S.T. Coleridge (d) Alfred Tennyson
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Ulysses' is a famous dramatic monologue by the Victorian poet Alfred, Lord Tennyson.

entries.question_text: Who wrote the poem ‘Ozymandias’?
entries.options_raw: (a) Thomas Hardy (b) Robert Frost (c) P.B. Shelley (d) Edmund Spenser
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Ozymandias' is a famous sonnet by the English Romantic poet Percy Bysshe Shelley, first published in 1818.

entries.question_text: Clym Yeobright is the protagonist of the novel—
entries.options_raw: (a) David Copperfield (b) Adam Bede (c) A Passage to India (d) The Return of the Native
entries.explanation: Explanation: Clym Yeobright is the central character in Thomas Hardy's novel 'The Return of the Native' (1878).

entries.question_text: The train is running ______ forty miles an hour.
entries.options_raw: (a) on (b) to (c) at (d) for
entries.explanation: Explanation: The preposition 'at' is used to indicate a specific speed, rate, or price.

entries.question_text: He divided the money ______ the two children.
entries.options_raw: (a) between (b) over (c) among (d) in between
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Between' is used when referring to two people or things. 'Among' is used for more than two.

entries.question_text: No one can______ that he is clever.
entries.options_raw: (a) defy (b) deny (c) admire (d) denounce
entries.explanation: Explanation: 'Deny' means to state that something is not true. The sentence means no one can say it's untrue that he is clever.
